account-pool-balanced.description: Keep coding across multiple accounts when one reaches its limit. Route Claude Code and Codex threads with quota-aware balancing, primary and reserve accounts, per-account caps, and session affinity. Connect Kimi, Z.AI, OpenCode Go, Cursor, and experimental Devin Local CLI; compatible external clients can use the proxy too. Bring your own provider accounts, subscriptions or API keys. Requires BB 0.43.1+ and Node/npm; disable BB's bundled Account Pooler because both register the same routes and command.

acp-profile-icons.description: Recognize eight ACP providers by their brand marks in model pickers and provider controls. Amp and Devin use contrasting theme-colored tiles; other marks follow the theme foreground, with a distinct gray tile for ACP Codex. Requires separately configured ACP providers and BB 0.44 or newer.

action-topbar.description: Keep open BB panel tabs within reach above every thread. Search tabs and Actions from one launcher, reorder tabs, close them in place, and drag Actions into panes. Requires BB 0.40+.

advisor.description: Adds a persistent second-model reviewer to BB coding threads, with tracked findings and fail-closed review status.

agent-board.description: Follow live BB agent activity, freshness, completion outcomes and monitoring health. Filter and group visible work by project, repository, provider or status. Optional Ollama Fleet and Redteam add worker visibility. Requires BB 0.40+; BB 0.46.0 recommended.

agent-calendar.description: See what your agents worked on and when, as a calendar of work blocks or a weekly time sheet. Each thread gets a block for the time its agent turns ran, colored by project, in a day, 3-day, or week view. Switch to Projects to merge a project's parallel threads into one entry, or open the time sheet to copy hours per thread and day as CSV. Agents can answer "what did my agents work on last week?" with the bb agent-calendar command and its bundled skill. Turn history stays in a local database on the bb server and uses no external service.

agent-graph.description: Shows your bb agents as a live node graph of threads, turns, tool calls, subagents and workflow agents, color-coded by type or status, so you can see what every agent is doing at a glance.

agent-icons.description: Give each BB agent provider its own icon and colour: built-in glyphs or your own SVG sets, synced across devices.

agent-lanes.description: See which agents are working, waiting for you, or failing across a live timeline. Follow hand-offs between threads, inspect any turn, and approve or reject requests on the block. Open Team lanes beside a thread or run bb lanes now for a text summary. Uses bb's local thread history, with no external account or API key.

agent-proxy.description: Runs CLIProxyAPI as a persistent macOS or Linux service, with OAuth account management, provider routing, usage stats, and one-step wiring for Claude Code and Codex.

agent-reload.description: Restart a thread's agent so it picks up MCP servers and config added after the thread started, without losing the conversation. Click the reload button in the thread header, and the agent answers your next message from a fresh session. Agents and scripts can do the same with bb agent-reload, including an agent reloading itself. Works with Claude Code, Pi, and ACP agents; Codex is not supported.

agent-retry.description: Retry a failed turn instead of accepting it as the end of the work. It retries any failure a provider reports, including one with no error classification at all — a gateway error, a process that died mid-stream, a request refused at the door — which bb's own retry declines. The wait grows with each attempt, up to 50 by default, and can be scoped by project, provider, thread, or the half of the failure space where the provider never took the request. Every decision is recorded with the rule behind it, and `bb agent-retry log`, `explain` and `simulate` show a retry before or after it happens. Disable BB's bundled Provider Retry plugin: both queue retries for the same failed turn.

agent-roles.description: Create reusable specialist profiles and start focused agent work. Optional Role Picker and Visual Workflows integrations. Agent work uses your configured provider account and quota.

agent-tools.description: Show which MCP servers and skills each BB machine actually has, then bring them to one catalogue and one canon. A matrix marks present, missing, and drifted configs; new servers wait for adopt, keep-local, or hide. Sync adds what is missing and never deletes on its own. The Skills tab treats ~/.agents/skills as a git canon, with fan-out into CLI homes and a version archive. Writes back up each config first; loopback paths and local secrets stay on that machine. Optional MetaMCP listing needs that gateway's API key.

agent-traces.description: See where your agents' time goes, from every thread down to each command, tool call, and subagent of a turn. A turn opens as a timeline that splits the agent's time into waiting on you, tools, subagents, thinking, writing, and model time, and it grows live while the agent works. Select a call to see its exit code, output, and arguments, or jump to the reply that followed it in the chat. A Traces page in the sidebar compares your recent threads by active time, calls, and errors, and two turns can be compared phase by phase. Turns export as OpenTelemetry or an HTML snapshot, and the bb agent-traces command gives agents the same answers. Traces come from the thread history on your bb server; an OpenTelemetry collector is optional.

agent-tv.description: See what every running agent is doing, and which one needs you, from a live wall at the foot of the sidebar. Each tile shows the tool call in flight, the files touched in the last minute, a 60-second activity trace, and how much of its context window the thread has used. Threads blocked on a question or an approval are marked and sorted to the top. Pop the wall out as a monitor you can drag anywhere in BB. The bb agent-tv status command gives terminals and agents the same feed, and nothing leaves your BB server.

agentic-mermaid.description: Draws Mermaid diagrams in chat with outlined boxes, routed edges, and your theme's colors. Renders 15 diagram types, including gantt, pie, mindmap, timeline, and architecture, through the agentic-mermaid library. Git graphs and types it can't draw keep bb's own renderer. Diagrams recolor when you switch between light and dark mode. Relies on bb internals, so a bb update can return diagrams to the stock renderer until the plugin catches up.

airbender.description: Keep your project's issues beside the agent doing the work. Track beads or GitHub issues, review plans and results, and start work in branches or worktrees. Run an epic's ready issues in sequence with Autopilot while keeping control of reviews and commits. Requires BB 0.44+; setup installs bend from GitHub Releases on Linux/macOS amd64 or arm64 using curl and SHA-256 tools, with Go 1.24+ needed for source builds on other platforms.

android-emulator.description: Watch and drive an Android emulator, a virtual phone, beside your thread, on the same device your agent controls. The panel streams the live screen with touch, scroll, keyboard and system buttons, and pastes Unicode text into the focused field. Agents list, start and stop AVDs and press keys through bb android-emulator commands. Needs a Windows or Linux bb host with the Android SDK and an existing AVD; the plugin installs nothing.

animation.description: Play technical diagrams as a sequence of beats, then export a looping HTML page. Open a .scene.json file to get a stage and a timeline: drag a step boundary to retime it, or click a part to quote its state into chat. Agents write the same JSON with ordinary file edits. GIF and MP4 export are not included; HTML is the shareable output. Requires BB 0.43 or later.

antigravity-cli.description: Code with your Antigravity account inside BB. Choose CLI-discovered models, switch between Plan and Build, and review tool requests in your thread. Requires a separately installed Antigravity CLI and an eligible account; service quota or charges apply. Tested locally on Windows.

archive-section.description: Move every thread you archive into an Archived sidebar section, and back to its old section when you unarchive it. The move happens right after the archive, from the sidebar, the CLI, or an agent, and children archived with a parent move too. Threads archived before install, or while the plugin was off, are swept in when it loads. Pick the section by name in settings; emoji and case are ignored, and the section is created if it does not exist.

archived-toggle.description: Show or hide archived threads in the sidebar with one click. An archive button in the sidebar footer adds archived threads to bb's thread list, and a second click removes them. It flips the same active/archived setting as Organize in the list, so the choice stays after a reload. Requires bb's built-in Thread list plugin to stay enabled.

asana.description: Work your Asana tickets inside bb: read them, start an agent thread from one, and hand it back when it's done. Your My Tasks list sits in the sidebar and beside every thread, in your own sections, with overdue and time-against-estimate badges. Opening a task shows its description, images, comments, subtasks, and editable fields, and a thread started from it begins with the ticket's details. Hand back posts your comment and reassigns the task to whoever filed it in one step, and agents need your approval before they write anything to Asana. Needs an Asana account and a personal access token.

attention-sidebar.description: Puts every thread that is waiting on you, from all projects, at the top of the bb sidebar. Questions and approvals, errors, and finished-but-unread threads share one block, each marked ?, ! or ✓. Running threads get their own block below it, and everything else sits in collapsible project folders with project avatars instead of provider icons. Block titles and labels are in Russian; the plugin is frontend-only and needs no external service.

audio-preview.description: Plays .m4a and other audio files in BB's file panel, including audio/mp4 that the built-in preview refuses.

auggie.description: Registers Augment Code's Auggie CLI as the acp-auggie provider in bb.

aura.description: Make your BB workspace your own with personal wallpapers, animated GIFs, and pixel textures. Save six backgrounds and switch in one click. Choose half or full wallpaper, keep the top bar clean or let the wallpaper continue behind it, and show an optional GitHub activity overview below the New thread composer. Images stay on your BB server; the activity overview uses the server's GitHub CLI login.

aura-motion.description: Play your own video, GIF or photo behind every BB conversation, with your messages on frosted glass so they stay readable. MP4 and WebM loops up to 24 MB play at up to 4K, and GIFs up to 8 MB play at their own frame timing. Choose Solid, Glass or Sheer for the message column: dark glass dims bright frames, phones get frosted cards so text stays readable, and Reduce Transparency turns it solid. Add an optional moving pixel-dither effect with seven patterns or five photo motions, and save six backgrounds to switch with one click. Images and videos stay on your BB server; the optional GitHub activity overview needs the GitHub CLI signed in on that server. A fork of Aura by Mateo Cerquetella; install it instead of Aura, not beside it.

auto-answer.description: Answers an agent's question with one click per question instead of two. A countdown starts the moment you pick an option, then presses the widget's own Next or Submit answer button. It appears under the option you picked and leads with a Stop button, and space or Escape stops it as well. Picking again, another option or the same one, restarts it from the full delay of 4 seconds, adjustable from 1 to 120. It never picks an option and never types free text, and it stands down by itself whenever pressing the button would be wrong, such as nothing selected or the free-text box open.

auto-compact.description: Compacts thread context automatically once usage reaches a configurable percentage, with a manual Compact button in every thread header.

auto-hide-panel.description: Give the thread its full width back when you close the last tab in the right panel. The panel hides itself as soon as its last file or other content tab closes. Info and Diff do not count, and Info you open yourself stays open. Loading the plugin or switching threads never hides the panel.

auto-pin.description: Keeps every thread you start pinned to the top of the sidebar, so a thread stays in reach until you unpin it yourself. Pins each visible top-level thread as it is created, and leaves child threads, hidden threads, and anything already pinned untouched. Unpinning still works the way it always did, so pin state stays yours to edit from the sidebar. Runs on thread creation with nothing to configure, no commands to learn, and no network access.

auto-router.description: Choose a coding model for each task and see where your tokens go. Route work to Codex or Claude Code, delegate helper tasks, and compare recorded usage with cost estimates. Experimental support targets macOS with BB 0.46.

automation-groups.description: Organize scheduled work into folders and control groups together. Inspect run history, errors and agent transcripts. Requires the bundled Automations plugin; agent runs use provider quota.

autoresearch-self-loop.description: Let an agent iterate on one measured metric in your Git checkout, and keep a log of every attempt. Each kept run becomes a commit with its result in the message, and a keep is refused when the benchmark or checks failed. A discarded, crashed, or checks-failed run reverts the agent's changes, including new untracked files that Git does not ignore. Needs Git, a committer identity, a clean working tree when a session starts, and a benchmark that prints METRIC name=value lines.

aws-activate-usage.description: Keep your AWS promotional-credit runway visible while agents work. View remaining balance, amount used, expiration dates, and current-month allocations in BB, with cached results when credentials expire. Reconnect an AWS SSO session from the same panel. Requires AWS CLI v2, a configured AWS profile, Billing permissions, and an AWS account with promotional credits.

ayu.description: Adds the three ayu themes (Light, Dark and Mirage) and a settings panel that switches between them and copies any colour from the palette.

backlog.description: Read and edit the Backlog.md files of your BB projects: a live Kanban board for tasks, and tabs for documents and decisions. Add selected text to the chat of the project with its file path. Needs BB 0.43 or later with Plugin SDK 0.5.9 or a later 0.5 version, and a Backlog.md folder on an enrolled host. No Backlog CLI or account is needed. Light theme only; tested on macOS.

bb-agent-toolbox.description: Gives any coding agent (opencode, Prime Agent, Google Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code, and more) direct tools for bb: read and edit workspace files, inspect and message other threads, delegate work by spawning threads, and see running terminals.

bb-antigravity-usage.description: See separate Antigravity weekly quota windows for Gemini and Claude/GPT models in BB. Reports each model family's quota and reset time from your local Antigravity login. Requires an existing Antigravity ACP provider and a local Antigravity account.

bb-autoresearch.description: Orchestrates autoresearch loops: parallel agent workers try code changes, and only the ones your benchmark proves better are kept. The plugin, not the agents, runs every measurement and decides each verdict from paired runs and confidence intervals, with guardrails on secondary metrics. A Live tab shows workers, candidates and each measurement's confidence band as they move, and any study can be replayed. Harvest turns the wins into draft PRs, each with its contribution measured by reverting it. Requires git 2.38 or newer; benchmarks run your repository's own commands, and the GitHub CLI is needed only to publish PRs.

bb-better-latex.description: Renders $...$ and leftover \[...\] / \(...\) math in BB chat.

bb-box.description: Give each thread its own Linux, Windows or macOS computer, or an iPhone or Android device, shared with its agent. You and the agent use the same desktop or terminal in BB's panel, and the agent waits while you have control. On the backends that support it, a snapshot saves a box before a risky change, and a restore with an undo or a fork brings it back. Boxes run on Docker, microsandbox, Proxmox, Tart on your Macs, or your own machines over SSH; Hetzner Cloud, Namespace and boat.dev need an account and bill you for what boxes use. Not a sandbox: BB Box assumes one trusted user.

bb-copilot-usage.description: See GitHub Copilot AI-credit or premium-request usage beside your other BB providers. Reads the quota shown by the authenticated Copilot CLI and reports the billing-cycle reset estimate. Requires GitHub Copilot CLI, a Copilot account, and tmux on the BB host.

bb-github-pr-dashboard.description: See why each pull request is stuck, and get it unstuck, without leaving bb. My PRs lists your pull requests, review requests for you and your teams, the ones you reviewed, and assigned ones by repository, each with its +/- lines and led by what blocks it: failing CI down to the job, changes requested, unresolved comments, conflicts or a stack. Reviewed turns amber when the author pushes after your review. Open one for its reviewers and their verdicts, labels, and tabs: Overview (the description, then comments and reviews), Checks with error annotations, Files with syntax-highlighted diffs and review threads under their lines, Commits with the ones since your review marked, and Comments. Edit the title and description, comment on a line or range, reply, delete your own comments, submit a review, mark your draft ready, and close or reopen, each only when you click. A menu links the PR to a bb thread, asks about it, explains it, or sends every finding to an agent, starting in the PR's project; Fix with agent does it for one comment or failed job. Jira keys open in bb's My Jira plugin. Search, hide or fold repositories, move by keyboard, switch gh accounts, and get alerts when CI fails or someone comments. Uses the GitHub CLI login or a token; github.com only.

bb-kujo.description: Give bb the paper-and-ink design of Kujo, with hard edges and quiet background signal. Switch between light and dark palettes with matching code, diffs and terminal colors. Departure Mono and Tabler icons carry the technical details. Requires bb 0.43; no external account or service.

bb-live.description: Talk to BB while your agents work, then redirect threads or start new project work by voice. Keeps one voice session connected while you move through projects, focus threads, and hear task results in the transcript. Explicit new tasks can start project threads or go to the BB Operator for coordination, while consequential actions stay in BB's visual approval flow. Requires BB 0.43.1+, Git, npm, Node.js 22.19+, an OpenAI project with GPT-Live access, and microphone permission; OpenAI usage is billed separately.

bb-office.description: Turns active BB threads into a draggable pixel-art office with live worker state, thread navigation, usage indicators, and agent-configurable behavior.

bb-recap.description: Generates concise, display-only summaries for BB threads on demand or after they become idle.

bb-rpiv-todo-renderer.description: Renders Pi rpiv-todo tasks in BB's native composer to-do panel.

bb-sidebar.description: A sidebar inspired by T3 Code that adds manual and automatic thread sorting, collapsible shelves, and bulk actions to bb.

bbbbs.description: Dial into a 1994-style bulletin board from bb to chat with other bb users and play classic multiplayer door games. Doors include Legend of the Red Dragon, Trade Wars 2, Usurper and Dice Warz, in shared worlds with daily turns and leaderboards. Your first call creates an account from a handle and a silly questionnaire; bb keeps the password, so there is no email or GitHub sign-in. Opted-in agents get their own [BOT] account and two tools to read the screen and press keys, limited to one chat line per 30 seconds and no board posts. Connects to the community server at bbs.gravytrain.ca, run by the author.

bbium.description: Click anything in bb without the mouse: press f, type the letter label, and bb clicks it. Labels cover sidebar threads, pickers, composer controls and hover-only message actions, and most stay one or two letters long. j and k scroll the chat, gg and G jump to its ends, and i puts the cursor back in the composer. Change hint letters, colors and fonts in settings or by asking an agent; changes apply live.

beads.description: Track issues and dependencies for long-running agent work with beads, so plans survive context loss. Agents call a beads tool to run bd prime, pick ready work, create tasks under epics, and record status changes in the thread's own checkout. A bb beads command runs any bd command from your shell. Requires the bd CLI installed separately on the BB host (brew tap steveyegge/beads && brew install bd).

beautiful-chat.description: Restyles BB's chat — composer, messages, work rows, loading states — in BeautifulUI's design language, using your active theme's colors.

beside.description: Turns the bb sidebar into an inbox where threads keep their place and finished work waits on shelves until it has news. Snooze, settle or mute a thread from its row or from bb's thread menu, and it comes back when it finishes, fails or asks you something. Child threads nest under their parent, and pinned threads drag into your own order. Shelf menus act in bulk with Undo. Optional rules settle threads after you read them, archive long-settled work, or ask a self-hosted decision model whether news needs you. Needs bb 0.46 or later.

boat.description: Run each bb thread on its own Boat cloud VM that stops when idle and resumes on demand. Start from the stock Ubuntu image or your own saved snapshot, and pick the VM size, Boat environment and org. Requires a Boat account (paid, billed per second) and a bb hub reachable from the internet.

bots.description: Adds a Bots panel to the BB sidebar where you create named bots with their own instructions, provider, model, reasoning level and optional project, then chat with them; each bot's instructions are bound per-thread, so a persona applies only inside that bot's own chats.

branch-graph.description: See how your repositories, branches, worktrees, and BB threads connect on one canvas. Search across registered Git projects, inspect selected checkouts, and flag detached or prunable worktrees for review. Optional GitHub PR lookup requires the gh CLI and authentication.

breathe.description: An animated pixel wave that guides your breathing while your agent works.

browser-copy.description: Copies what you point at in a BB Browser tab: pick any element and get a structured markdown block — page URL, viewport, CSS selector, ARIA role and name, bounds, link, and text — or a PNG of just that element, or a screenshot of the visible tab. One icon button in the thread header opens the three modes, and the picker outlines each target with a hover highlight and label as you move. Redaction is a heuristic on form fields — a password input, or a name, id or autocomplete matching password, credential, secret, token, api-key or auth — so it covers more than passwords but nothing outside an input, and images are not redacted.

browser-gestures.description: Swipe two fingers on the trackpad to go back and forward in the BB browser. A dark arrow slides in from the edge as you swipe, and the page changes when you lift your fingers; pull back to cancel. Vertical scrolling and horizontal scrollers that can still move keep working as before. Requires the BB desktop app and a trackpad.

browser-session-import.description: Signs every ordinary BB Browser tab into one imported cookie session. Import once from a local Chrome, Firefox, or other browser profile, or from a JSON cookie export, and the shared session carries those logins to existing and new tabs. Re-import any time to replace the session, and remove it with one button to clear the Browser. Cookies are read on this machine only; native profiles read on macOS and Linux, while JSON exports work anywhere the BB desktop runs.

browser-tools.description: Test websites from your agent and inspect what actually happened in the browser. Navigate, click and type using page snapshots, then review screenshots and browser errors. Requires BB 0.43 or later with a connected desktop browser and an agent provider; normal provider and website-account costs apply. Tested on macOS; other host operating systems remain unverified.

browserbase.description: Browserbase gives BB a real browser to use the web like a human. Navigate interactive websites, perform complex actions using natural language, and extract data from pages. Each BB thread gets its own cloud browser session. Requires a Browserbase account and API key; usage counts toward your Browserbase plan.

btrfs-cow.description: Start a thread with your installed dependencies, build caches, and uncommitted changes already in place. Each thread gets an independent checkout that shares disk blocks until files change, using Btrfs snapshots or reflink copies. Select Btrfs Cow in the environment picker; the plugin checks filesystem support on the chosen machine. Requires Linux, Git, GNU cp with reflink support, and a compatible filesystem such as Btrfs or XFS; snapshot mode also needs the btrfs command.

burn.description: See what every agent thread costs in dollars while it runs, per prompt and across all your threads. A chip beside the context circle shows the thread's total and what the last prompt added; click it for where the money went, a chart of every model call and the total with child threads. The Burn tab in the side panel lists the cost of each prompt, and a Burn page in bb's navigation charts spend across threads by day, project, model and harness. Budgets notify you at 80% and 100% of a thread's budget, and stop a run only if you turn that on. Works with pi, OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code and any harness that reports usage to bb; where a harness records no cost, Burn estimates it from list prices and marks it with ~.

cache-watch.description: See how much prompt caching each turn reuses and what its tokens would cost at Standard API rates. Expand the Cache panel for per-request reads and writes, first-request cache use, and estimated time left. Open the Cache marker under an assistant reply for saved turn details, or Session statistics for totals and turn history. Optional time-limited keepalive sends ordinary paid turns through your configured provider; cache hits and savings are not guaranteed. Requires BB 0.48+ and Plugin SDK 0.6.104+; Claude Code Telemetry support requires that separate provider plugin.

calm.description: A little world while your agent works. Sixteen pixel-art scenes bring sheep, sailboats, a rooftop cat, and forty-eight little misadventures to bb. An amber light means it needs you. A rain cloud marks an error. Requires bb 0.45 or later, with no external service or account.

captains-deck.description: Puts a first mate's whole crew on one board, so you only touch the calls that need you. Five columns track what is charted, what is underway, the decisions waiting on you, merges, and landings. Answer a call in place: pick an option, add a note, and the answer reaches the first mate's thread. Cards carry live thread state (working, queued, needs input, failed), the worker bot, and the pull request link. The first mate charts and moves work with the `bb deck` command; no external service or account is needed.

cascade.description: Shows active BB threads in a tiled layout with horizontal columns and vertical groups.

catchup.description: Shows a short recap above the composer, so you can pick up a thread without rereading it. Close it with × once you have read it; it stays closed on every device until a newer recap replaces it. Recaps follow the language of your latest messages, or one language you set. Other layouts add a compact banner, an expanded banner and a larger card. Each recap is a normal request to the provider you choose and never enters the thread's context.

change-gate.description: Approve production changes from a card that says what changes, where and how to undo it. Agents ask before a migration, a deploy or deleting shared data, and you answer with one click. An approval covers one request, and a decline tells the agent not to look for another route. Every decision stays in a journal page and in bb change-gate log. Agents are instructed to ask; the gate does not block other tools.

chat-dock.description: Write your next message beside the diff, file or tab you are reading: the composer moves into the right panel while it is open. Your draft and the cards above the box (running commands, child threads, questions) move with it and go back under the timeline when you close the panel. Dock it as a strip under whichever tab is open, or as a Chat tab of its own that splits and drags like any other. Split chat panes keep a composer each, and on a phone it docks at the bottom of the panel drawer. It moves BB's own page elements, which are not a documented interface, so a BB update may need a plugin update. Requires BB 0.48 or later.

chat-find.description: Press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on Mac) in any bb chat to find words in the conversation, with every match highlighted where it appears. Enter and Shift+Enter step through matches, and the chat scrolls each one clear of the composer, including matches inside bold text, links, and syntax-highlighted code. The count updates while an agent is still replying, without losing your place. Escape closes the bar and puts the cursor back where it was. It searches the messages the chat has loaded, leaves Ctrl+F to the embedded browser and terminals when they have focus, and needs no account or external service.

chat-sidebar.description: See which threads need you at a glance in a messenger-style sidebar with live status, folders, and project colours. Sub-agents and forks fold into their parent, so each task is one row. Attention, project, and section folders sit as tabs or a Telegram-style rail, each with unread badges, and you can add your own folders that pick chats by status, project, agent, or words in the title. Projects get distinct colours you can change, and the + starts a chat in the open project. Search, pinned order, splits, and bb's thread shortcuts all keep working.

chat-width.description: Give your conversations the room they need. Save separate Reading and Wide widths, or fill the current pane. Messages and the input stay aligned across split views and side panels. Preferences stay in this browser; no account or external service is required.

chief.description: Coordinates project supervisors that delegate work to managed worker and reviewer threads and follow it through completion.

chime.description: Plays configurable notification sounds when bb turns start, finish, fail, pause for a question, or request approval.

claude-account-switcher.description: Switches one BB Claude Code thread to the verified Claude subscription login on its machine while preserving thread history.

claude-switcher.description: See every Claude Code account in one usage panel, pick the account before a new thread's first message or from any thread's header, start new projects on the best account, and move a project to a free account when a turn hits a subscription limit. Runs on macOS and Linux, on the machine that holds your Claude Code logins.

claude-theme.description: Give BB terracotta accents with charcoal dark and off-white light palettes. Select one palette that follows Light, Dark or System, with matching syntax and terminal colours. Adapted from SK's Claude Theme for VS Code, with accents on selected navigation and active tabs. Requires BB 0.47.1 or later and a compatible Plugin SDK; no account or external service is needed.

claude-usage.description: See how much of your Claude plan is left and where your AI coding spend went, by session, day and model, across every agent CLI you use. Each limit window shows what is left, when it resets and where you will land at your current pace, with a plain verdict on whether there is room for a big task. Sessions carry their titles and projects; open one for its models and its cost by token type, or click a model to filter the whole page. Reads Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the other CLIs ccusage supports from their local logs, and draws each provider in its own colour. Prices come from LiteLLM's public price list, so a newly released model is priced without a plugin update. Plan limits use the Claude Code sign-in already on your machine and need a Claude subscription.

cli-agents.description: Start each chat with a specialist agent or selected profile instructions. Choose native Claude Code and OpenCode agents, or Codex profile developer instructions (up to 4096 characters; other profile settings are not applied), in new chats and handoffs on local or enrolled remote machines. Requires BB 0.43.0 or later on macOS or Linux and an installed, authenticated supported CLI; provider subscription limits or API charges apply.

clickable-local-link.description: Opens a local document from a chat link in its Mac app, and a folder link in Finder, with one click. Text and code files keep BB's preview, and Option-click selects any linked item in Finder. Scripts, apps and unknown file types are only selected, never opened, including when a link hides them behind a symlink. A bundled skill tells agents to write local paths as clickable links. Works in the macOS desktop app on the Mac that runs BB.

code-review-workspace.description: Understand a pull request or local diff before you approve it, and post a review you edited from an agent's draft to GitHub. An agent splits the change into chapters in reading order, rates each one's risk, and points to the one to three lines most likely to hide a defect. The review agent drafts line comments with a severity, a summary, and a suggested verdict, and you choose what posts to GitHub. All reviews sorts your PRs by whose turn it is, and after new commits Since your review shows only what changed and checks each of your earlier comments. Review a BB thread's uncommitted work the same way, then send your comments back to the thread that wrote the code. Needs git and a signed-in GitHub CLI (gh) on the BB server, works with github.com only, and spends your BB agent provider's usage on guides and reviews.

codex-realtime.description: Run Voice Mode's voice chats on your ChatGPT subscription instead of a separately billed OpenAI API key. It hands Voice Mode the ChatGPT sign-in that the Codex CLI already keeps on the machine running the bb server, reads it again for every chat, and never renews or rewrites it. Only the plugins you allow, Voice Mode to begin with, receive the token; the bb app, the command line and agents in threads never do. This is an undocumented use of the subscription that OpenAI could stop accepting at any time, nobody has checked whether OpenAI's terms allow it, and voice chats count against your ChatGPT plan. Requires bb 0.46 or later, Voice Mode 0.1.9 or later, and the Codex CLI signed in with Sign in with ChatGPT on a plan that includes Codex.

codex-theme.description: Brings the OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT desktop app's look to bb: system-font typography at 430 weight, the Codex surface and menu geometry, its send arrow, and a roomier left rail. Pick Catppuccin or BB's own colors, and turn on optional changes in the plugin settings. Light and dark.

collapsible-navigation.description: Folds the sidebar navigation upward into a compact strip to maximize vertical space for your thread list. Quick actions remain accessible with one click in the collapsed bar, and navigation icons can optionally move into the window top header. Remembers expanded and collapsed state across restarts.

command-code.description: Runs BB threads on any of Command Code's 70 coding models, so a bug has to survive reviewers on Claude, GPT, GLM, Kimi or DeepSeek without leaving BB. Shell commands, file reads and edits arrive as BB timeline cards with streamed output and diffs, and reasoning stays separate from the reply. Needs Command Code installed and signed in, plus the adapter this repository ships. Command Code's headless mode cannot prompt per tool call, so writes are one setting rather than a per-call approval.

compact-nav.description: Make more room for threads with compact, borderless sidebar icons. Keep your saved order and hidden destinations, with controls to rearrange or show them. Hover labels and selected states keep navigation recognizable. Requires BB 0.42+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.53+, with no extra service or account.

companion-chat.description: Opens a fresh hidden thread beside the current BB conversation with independent provider and model selection, keeping it out of the sidebar unless the user later makes it visible.

composer-autocollapse.description: Keep the prompt box compact when you click away or leave it idle, with drafts left in place. Set the focus-out delay and idle timeout, while editor, toolbar, model-picker and menu interactions stay open. Idle collapse requires focus inside the box and an empty draft, or a hidden tab when that option is enabled. Requires BB 0.49.0+.

composer-predictions.description: Suggests the message you're likely to send next as ghost text in the empty composer, one Tab from an editable draft. Nothing is sent for you: Tab only fills an empty message box, and typing, pasting or Escape hides the suggestion until the conversation moves on. Suggestions are saved across restarts and checked against the conversation before they reappear, so an unchanged thread costs no new request. Every reply in a thread you've opened costs one request in a hidden helper thread, which receives up to 48,000 characters of recent messages and tool output.

conductor-theme.description: Applies the Conductor workspace aesthetic across bb with roasted espresso and native black surfaces, warm brown message cards, bone typography, and emerald accents.

context-handoff.description: Track context usage as a percentage and safely continue long tasks in fresh threads. A meter above the chat input shows how full the context window is: it uses your theme's main color below 20% (light gray in dark mode), then turns yellow at 20%, orange at 30%, red at 40% and dark red at 65%. Each thread has an Auto handoff switch, off until you turn it on. Turn it on below 20% and the thread hands off once it reaches 30%; turn it on at 20% or above and it hands off at the next safe stopping point. The agent saves its plan and progress as notes, and a fresh thread confirms it read them, then continues with the switch on. Turning the switch off cancels a pending handoff.

context-health.description: See what contributes to your thread’s context usage. Search recorded text, inspect observed skill reads and browse available skills. Optional Codex session detail reads logs on the thread host; no separate account or paid service is required.

copilot-aic-usage.description: Track Copilot AI credits in your BB thread. See this session's usage, today's host total, and monthly premium requests. Install the GitHub Copilot provider from BB's marketplace and sign in to GitHub Copilot CLI with a Copilot-enabled account.

copilot-session-credits.description: Track reported GitHub Copilot credit usage for each BB thread. Click the indicator to see the amount, coverage, and capture status or get Pi setup instructions. Copilot CLI works directly with the official registry provider and supported custom variants; Pi requires a separate companion extension and Pi 1.5.0+. Requires authenticated GitHub Copilot access; tested on macOS. Pi coverage is partial, so earlier calls and hidden retries may be missing.

cortado.description: Neutral graphite with warm orange and amber, in light and dark. Three palettes: one that follows bb's light or dark mode, and fixed dark and light versions. Recolors the app, the syntax colors in chat, diffs and file previews, and the terminal.

crew.description: Run a standing team of agents that message each other, hand off work and wait for you only when they need an answer. You describe the team once in a crew.yaml: each member gets a fixed address, its own provider and model, a role and its own worktree, and every member is a thread in the sidebar. Several crews in one project coordinate through their leads, BB Tasks and the base branch, with a step limit so they cannot loop forever. A project overview shows who works, who waits and every cross-crew message. Merge and rebase need the repository on the machine BB runs on.

cua-driver.description: Gives bb agents background desktop and Chromium browser control, powered by the open-source Cua Driver from Cua AI, with per-provider routing.

cursor-sidebar.description: See at a glance which agents are working, which need an answer and which are done, with spawned chats nested under their parent. Group chats by project, last update, status or environment, or draw one flat list, and narrow every grouping to one project from the switcher. With the Projects plugin, a worker opens as a tab of its project lead, so the lead's side panel stays in view. After install the sidebar switches to the Cursor navigation layout, and Compact is one setting away. Give each project a glyph in one of ten colours or an uploaded PNG, filter by status, age, environment or pull request, and spot chats on cloud machines by their cloud mark. Needs BB 0.49 or newer; no account or external service.

dashboard.description: Keep project conversations, live activity and application shortcuts in one workspace. Read and continue chats, search project history and switch conversations with bottom tabs. Track work and requests for attention across projects, open applications alongside your workspace and choose English or Russian. Requires BB 0.48+ and internet access for first-install dependencies; no separate service, account or API key.

deepseek-harness.description: Run DeepSeek Harness (dsh) threads in bb over ACP, with Standard, Creator, and Minimal modes chosen in the New thread composer, a read-only badge naming the mode a thread booted with, a live roster of the dsh subagents a thread deploys, harness slash commands exposed to the agent, and one-command provisioning of the dsh profiles, run_command plugin, and ACP bridge patch. Requires dsh installed globally and a model credential for its route.

dependabot.description: Reviews GitHub Dependabot alerts grouped by dependency and sends grouped fixes to BB agents.

design-director.description: Catch a screen that looks generic before you call the work done, and keep every design score on record. A critic scores each screenshot without seeing the code, so the agent that built the screen is not the one grading it. Three tiers run from a single-call spot check after any UI change to a full redesign with seeded directions and critic rounds. Critic runs spend tokens on your own provider account, at a cost that depends on the model you pick, and the screenshot scripts need Chrome or Chromium and Node 18 or newer.

desktop-browser-agent.description: Lets your agents use the apps and browser tabs on your machine in the background, while you keep working. Agents read and operate native apps and Chrome, Edge or Brave windows through Cua Driver from Cua AI, which the settings page installs and checks on each machine. The optional Browser Bridge for bb extension lets them work in any tab of your signed-in browser, in an Agent tab group you can pause. Tools that run code or force-quit apps start off, and agents can be made to ask before clipboard, screen capture and file actions. Needs Cua Driver (free, MIT). Tested on macOS 14+; Windows 10/11 and Linux with X11 are supported by Cua Driver but not yet tested with this plugin.

dictation-shortcuts.description: Dictate into a BB draft by holding Space, then release to finish. Enter finishes recording without sending, Escape cancels, and Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles recording without holding a key. Microphone tooltips and modifier-held badges show the controls beside BB’s native buttons. Requires BB 0.46.1+, microphone permission and an available BB voice-input service; that service’s existing account requirements and charges still apply, with no additional speech service installed.

diff-explorer.description: Review every changed file in one scroll, and ⌘-click any symbol to read its definition without leaving the diff. Press Ctrl+- to step back, so you can follow a call several levels deep and return to the hunk you were reading. Switch between uncommitted changes and all changes since the base branch. Open it with ⌘⇧D or the button in the thread header. Go to definition needs the language server on your PATH: gopls, rust-analyzer, pyright, clangd, or sourcekit-lsp; TypeScript downloads typescript-language-server through npx on first use.

diff-plus.description: Improves BB's Diff tab with a folder tree beside the file list: file counts and +/- per folder, sticky folders, Tree or Flat view, compact folders, a view synced with the list, and your recent commits in the scope picker. It works through the tab's own filter, so BB's search, Viewed marks, split view and Add to chat work as before. Requires BB 0.48 or later; it finds the Diff tab by its page structure, so a BB update may need a plugin update.

diff-review.description: Comment on a thread's changes line by line, then send the comments to its agent, which fixes the code and answers each one. A Review tab beside the thread shows the diff of its uncommitted, staged or unstaged changes, its branch, one commit or a range, and each comment follows its code as the code moves. The same tab reviews a GitHub pull request: answer its threads, mark files viewed in step with GitHub, and submit your comments as one review, posted as the GitHub CLI's signed-in account. An AI review leaves comments of its own, @reviewer answers a question inside a comment thread, and Fix in a new thread hands the comments to another agent; these runs start as threads under the one being reviewed, in the permission mode set in the settings (bb's Approve for me by default, or Accept edits), and in full permission mode with a provider that lacks that mode, such as opencode. Follows the review loop of the open-source diffity, credited in the plugin's third-party notices. Needs bb 0.48 or later with bb's Git plugin on, and the signed-in GitHub CLI (gh) for pull request review only; it is built on experimental bb plugin APIs that may change between bb releases.

diff-tree.description: Review Git changes by folder and bring selected code into your BB chat. Compare branch changes, the working copy, recent commits, or a single commit in unified or split view. Expand unchanged context and add file mentions without sending the draft. Requires BB 0.46.1+, SDK 0.6.49+, and Git on the workspace host; no external service or account is needed.

disk-usage.description: Shows what's taking up disk space on the bb server host, ncdu-style, with drill-down by directory and a bb disk-usage CLI.

doc-review.description: Comment on documents, spreadsheets, and web pages beside the chat, then hand every comment to an agent in one message. Select text in Markdown, PDF, Word, or PowerPoint files, box a chart on a page or slide, pick spreadsheet cells, or click any element of an HTML page; a comment on an area reaches the agent with an image of that region. Draw over a prototype or page to cross out a button, frame a block, or point an arrow to where it should move, and the agent gets the page as you saw it with your strokes on top. Each comment shows whether the agent closed it with a note on what changed or answered with a question, and a thread under it carries the conversation for as many rounds as it takes. In the bb desktop app, a Review button beside the browser's address bar puts the same comments on a live site, where they stay on their pages across reloads and deploys. Download a PDF with your comments as annotations any PDF viewer shows; Doc Review in another bb imports them, so a colleague can answer and send the file back. Files attached to chat messages open in the same tab, and the tab works in bb's mobile web app. Needs poppler-utils and LibreOffice on the machine the bb server runs on; Chrome or Chromium there adds the pictures of drawings on HTML pages.

dockside.description: Organizes BB threads into compact project-first families with semantic status, inline child agents, persistent drag ordering, and mobile active-thread navigation.

drmanhattan.description: Makes agents in parallel threads take turns on builds and tests, and shows each thread its queued runs. Threads on a machine with drmanhattan, a local job queue, are told to run heavy commands through it, so several agents stop compiling at the same time and slowing each other down. While a thread has runs going, a row above its composer shows each run's slot or place in line against its usual time, with a cancel button and a link to its log; the Info tab lists recent results. A drmanhattan page in bb's navigation shows the queue on every connected machine, each run linked to the thread that queued it, and archiving a thread stops the dev servers it started. Agents and scripts also get bb drmanhattan runs, status and cancel. Needs the free, open-source drmanhattan command-line tool on each machine (macOS or Linux); the drmanhattan page installs and starts it with one click, showing the commands first.

droid.description: Registers Factory.ai's Droid CLI as the acp-droid provider in bb.

dynamic-file-tree.description: Browse the active project beside every BB thread, with Git status, previews, diff counts, and live agent activity. Navigate files and folders scoped to the current Environment or Worktree. Preview text, Markdown, and image files inside BB. See reads, writes, added, deleted, and changed files with configurable colors and metadata. Requires BB 0.48+ and a thread with an available Environment; it uses no external service or account.

e-corp.description: Turns bb into a cold corporate workstation, lit by one continuous petroleum-blue field that every panel shares. Dark and light are the same room at two exposures, so switching modes changes the light and not the design. Bundled Pierre-compatible code themes carry the palette into code, diffs, the file tree, and the terminal, with separate focus, selection, warning, and destructive colours. IBM Plex Sans and Mono and the texture are embedded in the stylesheet, so the theme makes no network requests.

elephant-goldfish.description: Runs a fresh-context review on every Markdown spec and applies only the changes you explicitly approve. Spec files stay as plain Markdown in your project checkout, listed on a dedicated spec workspace page and in a tab beside each conversation. Seven agent skills cover the workflow from brainstorm and draft through staged reviews, findings and proposals to resolution and drift reports. Reviews run as BB workers on the provider configured for the reviewed project, or as a tool-less OpenAI-compatible endpoint that needs a base URL, model id and API key.

env-catalog.description: Store API keys, tokens, and secrets in a single encrypted catalog across all BB sessions and machines. Securely request credentials via masked in-app modals. Agents automatically check available credentials before prompting you, and persist newly provided keys on demand. Values are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and synchronized via your central BB server. Includes dedicated agent tools, a full-featured management UI with .env import/export, and terminal CLI commands.

extella.description: Lets agents reuse programs that earlier threads already wrote: search them by meaning, run them on your machine, save new ones. A thread that asks in different words still finds the saved program and runs it without writing code. Programs run on your computer through Extella Desktop and can read local files there; a run takes about 10 seconds. Later threads and other bb projects that use the same Extella agent see the same library. Needs an Extella account with an API key and agent id, and Extella Desktop on the machine that runs programs.

factory.description: Turn requests into reviewed pull requests: a Lead plans tasks, specialist agents build them, and independent agents review each PR. A Factory page in the left rail shows every agent's live status and a board from Backlog to Done. When a builder finishes, the Lead opens a draft PR; Reviewer 1 and a Security reviewer start within about two minutes, plus Reviewer 2 for large or sensitive diffs, and each posts its verdict on the PR. The PR is marked ready for review only when every reviewer approves, and merging stays with you. Needs a Git project, the agent CLIs you choose per role (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor), and a GitHub remote with the gh CLI for PR review; optional Rafter scans need a Rafter account.

fast-archive.description: Archive finished conversations from the thread header. Uses BB’s archive and restore behavior, and avoids duplicate buttons when native archiving is present.

fast-split.description: Open a neighboring New thread pane from the sidebar footer. Keep the current pane visible while starting another conversation. Available in wide layouts, up to BB’s pane limit.

fat-fingers.description: Makes every icon in bb 50% larger on your phone, so a thumb has something to see and something to hit. Applies under the same phone test bb uses for its own touch sizing, so a desktop window with a mouse is left exactly as it was. Scales the icon's layout box rather than painting it larger, so the button around it grows to fit. Leaves diagrams and images inside messages at their normal size. Works in the bb mobile app and in a phone browser, with nothing to configure and no network access.

feed.description: See every thread that needs your answer in one list, each with a one-line summary of its latest result. Rows sort into Needs your response, In progress, and Paused, and you reply, pause, archive, or move a thread from its row. A bundled manager skill starts new work in a section the Feed watches and flags child results for you. Summaries use your Codex login (ChatGPT account or OpenAI API key); without it, a row shows the first sentence of the agent's latest message.

file-gateway.description: Browse files across your BB machines and FTP/SFTP sites, then add the right file to a chat. Preview folders and media, download individual files or a folder’s visible files as a ZIP, and insert native file mentions without exposing account passwords to agents. Requires connected BB machines or reachable website accounts; macOS/Linux, read-only website access, 256 MiB between BB hosts and 32 MiB from websites. English interface with drag-to-chat mentions and hidden-file controls.

file-manager.description: Manage the files on the machine bb runs on without a terminal: browse, upload, move, rename, extract and hand them to the agent. Opens as a sidebar page, as a tab beside a thread that can start in that thread's folder, and from a file link in a message. Double-click shows images, PDF, video, Markdown and code; Space looks inside zip, tar, 7z and rar archives without extracting them. Multi-gigabyte uploads resume after a dropped connection, and several files or a whole folder download as one zip. On a phone, selected rows get an Actions bar with the whole row menu. Access stays inside the home folder of the user bb runs as; tar, 7z and rar archives need tar and 7z on that machine.

file-pretty.description: Read structured files with consistent formatting inside BB. Switch between formatted and raw content, and copy the view on screen. Parse errors show their location in the file. Supports JSON, JSON Lines, YAML, TOML, XML, and XML-based formats. Formatting TOML omits comments; the raw view retains them.

file-versions.description: See which copy of a deck, document or spreadsheet is the latest across all your projects. Groups v2, final, dated and (1) copies of one document, in English and Russian. Copies in archive folders never count as the latest ahead of a current one. Agents get the same answer from bb file-versions list, so they work from the right file. Reads project folders on the BB server and never changes a file.

files.description: Browse and safely edit files in the current BB thread environment.

files-editor.description: A VS Code-style file explorer and editor for the workspace behind a thread. Search in files finds a word across every file in the project: results are grouped by file with each hit highlighted, and clicking one opens the file on that line. It is smart case, with match-case, whole-word and regex toggles, and built for typing — file contents stay in memory between searches, so refining a query re-runs in tens of milliseconds, and a regex runs in its own worker so a runaway pattern cannot freeze BB. Around it: a file tree that shows dotfiles, editor tabs, a go-to-file palette (Cmd+P), find in the open file (Cmd+F), syntax highlighting in your BB code theme, and edit and save guarded so a change an agent made underneath you is never clobbered. Markdown files open rendered, with the source and the editor one click away. Two pickers choose the project and then its checkout or one of its worktrees; beside a thread it is pinned to that thread's worktree. Adds a `bb files` command so agents can browse and read the same workspace from the CLI, on whichever machine it lives.

firstmate.description: Turn one thread into a crew: dispatch parallel agent ships in their own worktrees and land their work when it reports DONE. Ships get isolated git worktrees, scouts stay read-only, and every crew ends with a DONE, BLOCKED, or FAILED verdict. Thread events ping you the moment a crew finishes, fails, or stalls, and a crew that idles without a verdict gets nudged until it reports. Queue work with dependencies, gate merges behind green checks, and hand whole projects to domain captains. Requires the bb CLI on the host; the optional real firstmate toolbelt clones upstream firstmate scripts.

firstmate-crew.description: Hand one agent your to-do list and it runs a crew of worker threads, each in its own git worktree, until the work lands. The first mate is a pinned thread in bb's own chat that writes each worker's instructions, supervises it, and brings back branches, pull requests, findings and only the decisions that are yours. A FirstMate tab shows the crew as a board of Queued, Working, Blocked, Parked, Done, Failed and Idle, with Steer, Interrupt, Relaunch and End on every card. A built-in watch tells the first mate within about five minutes when a pull request is merged, reviewed or changes check status. Requires bb 0.47 or later, git, and the logged-in gh CLI for the pull request watch; a capable model such as Claude Sonnet is recommended for the first mate.

flare.description: Let an agent tell you what it found while it is still working, not only in the message that ends its turn. Agents get a `flare` tool and send a finding, a decision, a progress or status update, a blocker or a summary; the newest one shows in a banner above the message box, and the thread's Flares tab keeps them all, drawn the way bb draws a reply, so an agent can answer with a chart, a diagram, a table or a snippet instead of describing it. Blockers, and flares the agent marks urgent, send a push notification, so alerts reach you while the work carries on. A child thread's flares appear in its parent's tab, and a child's blocker reaches the parent's agent as a note without starting a turn. The tool returns at once, so the agent never waits, and `bb flare send` works from a terminal or another agent.

flexible-worktrees.description: Turns a pull request, branch, or new task into a ready worktree for the thread, with no Git commands to type. One picker searches open PRs, local and remote branches, and existing checkouts, then says exactly what launching will do. New branches start from the freshly fetched default branch, and PRs, including ones from forks, open as detached review worktrees. Worktrees go where your path template puts them, get their submodules and .worktreeinclude files, and are never deleted. Requires BB 0.43+ and Git 2.31+ on the selected machine; the GitHub CLI is optional, for listing PRs.

flexoki.description: Read and write on warm paper and ink with Flexoki by Steph Ango (kepano/flexoki): light and dark palettes, syntax and terminal colours.

floating-notes.description: Keep a note beside the work it belongs to, one keystroke from any thread. Notes group themselves by project, thread and day, so nothing lands in a flat pile. Stickies pin to a thread or a project and appear only while you are looking at it, and every thread gets a scratchpad your agents can append findings to. Writes real markdown — clickable checklists, highlighted code fences, wiki links — and stores everything in a local SQLite file with no account and no network.

floating-terminal.description: Adds a draggable terminal window over bb, opened from the sidebar footer or Ctrl+`, with a tab per shell in any project checkout or machine home directory; tabs are persisted, so a reload or a bb restart reattaches to the same shells with their scrollback.

focus-board.description: A kanban of your bb threads, focused on what needs you first. Group threads by attention, last activity, project, provider, machine, or parent; drag to act — hand-order a column, change a card's state in the drag, or nest a child; sweep stale lanes, snooze threads, and search titles, projects, and branches. Cards show state, pin, pending-interaction badge, update time, and branch or host; a click opens the thread and a modified click opens it in a new window.

focus-mode.description: Read a conversation as plain text, with tool calls, file edits, and every panel out of sight. Your prompts appear as quiet quotes and the agent's replies in one narrow column, refreshed every two seconds while the agent works. A small dot shows when the agent is running, and older history loads on request. Open it from the thread header or command palette, assign a shortcut in BB's Keyboard settings, and press Escape to return to your unchanged layout and draft.

focus-sidebar.description: Keeps only the threads from the last few hours in your sidebar and moves older ones to an Archive grouped by day. Threads that are running, waiting for your answer or pinned stay in Focus whatever their age, and you pick the window: 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours. A search box matches titles, projects and branches as you type, then message text across open and closed threads. Every row and the thread header get a close button that uses bb's own archive with Undo; nothing is archived automatically.

followups.description: Turn a finished answer into your next message: pick one of its suggested follow-ups and get a full draft in the composer. When a thread finishes, a model reads its last answer and your last three messages, then shows two to five next steps above the message box, each with the reason it is worth doing. Click one, or press 1–9, and it is written out as a first-person message in your composer; nothing is sent for you, and anything you typed stays. A switch in each thread's header turns follow-ups on or off for that thread, and a footer shows how long each run took and how many tokens it used. Each suggestion and draft is a short run on a model you choose from your bb providers, in a hidden worker thread that uses the provider's least privileged permission mode and is deleted when it finishes.

fonts.description: Choose local font families and tune interface, code, and serif typography independently of BB's active theme. Each role inherits size, weight, style, line height, and letter spacing from the theme until you override it, with live specimens before you save. Search the fonts installed on the device you view BB from, or type any family name. Installed-font discovery needs a secure desktop Chromium context; generic and manually entered families work everywhere, and no font data leaves the client.

forage.description: Put web research in every agent's hands and keep what it found in a per-thread Research tab you can read, quote and cite. web_search, web_fetch, web_map, web_extract, web_crawl and web_diff run as bb's own tools for every provider, with routing profiles, domain and date filters, bounded limits and every partial failure in words. Replies carry citation cards that quote the exact kept lines a claim rests on, and Check in sources matches any message against the pages stored for that thread. A zero-turn CLI runs the same operations; private networks are blocked by default and keyless DuckDuckGo and Exa search need no account.

fx.description: Run the fx coding agent in BB threads. Pick models available to your account, follow replies and tool activity, and resume sessions. Requires the fx CLI and an authenticated fx account; model access and charges depend on your provider.

genui.description: Turns agent replies into charts, diagrams, maps, plans and forms you can use, right in the chat. Agents choose from 86 components on their own, with no setup: sliders and filters recompute in the page, and buttons, choices and forms put your answers in your message, which reaches the agent when you send it. Test reports, logs, lint errors and coverage files render as their own components instead of pasted text, and a thread's changes, commits, pull request and workers are read live from BB. Adds about 6,400 tokens of instructions to sessions whose replies you read, and looks up photos, places and map tiles on Wikimedia Commons, Wikipedia, Photon and OpenStreetMap unless you turn web lookups off. Relies on BB internals, so a BB update can show the blocks as code until the plugin catches up.

gh-copilot.description: Registers GitHub Copilot CLI as the acp-gh-copilot provider in bb.

gh-projects-board.description: See what you are actually working on, in the columns your team already agreed on. The board reads the Status field of a GitHub Projects v2 board, so Todo, In Progress and QA arrive in the project's own order with each option's description, instead of every assigned issue landing in one pile. A My Tasks filter opens on your own unfinished work, and GitHub's filter syntax works as it does on github.com, including assignee:@me and negation. Group by any single-select field, not only Status. Requires the GitHub CLI signed in on the machine running the BB server, with a classic token carrying the read:project scope, because fine-grained tokens cannot read user-owned projects.

gh-stack.description: Visualizes and drives stacked pull requests from a bb thread panel, wrapping the gh stack CLI for split, push, submit, and merge.

ghostrunner.description: Turn BB into a cyberpunk console with near-black panels, a hot red accent, cyan for success and diffs, and yellow for warnings. Text uses JetBrains Mono and titles Chakra Petch, with a monospace fallback, and code previews get matching syntax colours. Dark only. No wallpapers are bundled: the overview links some that suit the theme, which you can set with Aura.

gigaam.description: Dictate in Russian with the bb microphone and get punctuated text, recognized on your own machine. On first load the plugin installs GigaAM v3, Sber's open Russian speech model, with a private Python and CPU-only PyTorch, so nothing is set up by hand. A 10-second phrase takes about 1 second on a 10-core CPU, and recordings over 20 seconds are split at pauses, so minute-long voice notes work. Audio never leaves the machine, or you can point the plugin at your own OpenAI-compatible transcription server. Needs Linux (x86-64 or arm64) or macOS on Apple silicon, about 2 GB of disk, 1.5 GB of RAM, and a one-time 1.2 GB download; recognizes Russian only.

git-graph.description: Follow branches, merges, and commit history beside your BB thread. Browse up to 200 commits with branch and tag labels, switch between configured repositories, and inspect history from the CLI. Runs Git in the thread's local or connected remote environment without changing the repository. Requires BB 0.47.1+, Git in the environment, and npm for installation; no external account or paid service is needed.

git-history.description: Shows the complete Git history of a project as a compact commit graph with changed files and per-file diffs.

git-panel.description: Git for the thread's workspace: stage, AI-commit, branch, and sync without leaving BB.

gitea.description: Manage Gitea issues and pull requests from BB. Review diffs, discuss changes, and handle labels, assignments, and status from a thread panel or the bb gitea command. Turn on Auto-fix or Auto-merge from My PRs or Pull requests. Install the tea CLI and sign in to your Gitea instance; agent actions use your configured BB model and tea permissions.

github-actions.description: Watch every GitHub Actions run of your BB projects, start any workflow with its inputs, and hand failures to an agent. A failed job opens its log at the error line, and Ask agent starts a thread with that excerpt and a brief to find the root cause. Run workflow turns a workflow_dispatch trigger into a form with branch, choice, and boolean inputs, checked before the request reaches GitHub. Rerun failed jobs, cancel a run, or send a run report to the BB threads you pick and subscribe them to new failures. Requires a GitHub account: the plugin uses the gh CLI login on the BB server machine, or a token you set.

github-app-auth.description: Run your bb agents as a GitHub App, so pull requests and commits open under the app's name and you can review them on GitHub. Each agent turn gets a short-lived installation token as GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, so gh and git act as the app. Commits use the app's bot identity and pushes go over the token. Enable only the projects you choose, with the scopes you grant the app, and personal projects stay yours. Needs a GitHub App you create and the gh CLI on the machines that run threads.

github-board.description: See your GitHub issues, pull requests and discussions on one board, and hand any of them to an agent thread. Four columns cover what you wrote, what is open on repositories you own and what is assigned to you, and an issue that a pull request closes folds into that pull request's card. Pull request cards show CI checks and branch status, with an Update branch button wherever you can push. A detail panel shows the body, comments and images, and labels are added or removed from a right-click menu. Send to chat opens bb's new-thread composer on a card, with a prompt you set per column and per project, in the bb project that has the repository checked out. Add to chat puts the same prompt, the card's column template with the chat's project override, at the end of a chat's draft without sending it, from a menu of the chats on screen and your recent threads. Requires bb 0.47 or later, and the GitHub CLI (gh) installed and signed in on the machine running the bb server.

github-extended.description: Browses cached GitHub issues, pull requests, and Dependabot alerts in BB with thread actions and agent-assisted work.

gitlab.description: Browses GitLab issues and merge requests in a BB panel, with pipelines, approvals, discussions and diffs, and spawns an agent thread on any of them.

gitlab-interface-notion-style.description: Review, merge and fix GitLab merge requests without leaving BB. Each merge request opens on a readiness strip that names what blocks it, and counts approvals and 👍 reactions as review. Reply to and resolve threads, read a failed job's log and retry it, or start a pipeline on any branch. Requires the glab CLI logged in to your GitLab host.

goals.description: Keep your personal priorities available when you ask an agent to evaluate an idea or plan. Reorder goals and archive completed ones. Goals do not launch work automatically. Agent evaluations use your configured provider quota.

gone-fishing.description: Turn the wait for your agent into a pixel-art fishing trip on top of the chat input. The pond fishes by itself while a turn runs, or you take the rod to hook, reel, and land each fish yourself. Water floods the chat input behind your text, and the fish swimming there are the ones that bite. Three maps hold 28 species, and the seasons follow your calendar. Your catches unlock new maps and gear for your angler, boat, and dog. Catches stay in a local database on the bb server and use no external service.

google-antigravity-acp.description: Adds Google Antigravity as a bb agent provider through its official ACP server (agy_acp_server.par), with the same provider bridge as bb's built-in ACP agents.

graph-studio.description: Build agent loops that go back when review fails, run them on real BB threads, and watch every step live. A node spawns a thread rather than calling a model, so workers appear in the sidebar and run on the providers you already have. Describe a flow in the chat and the agent builds and starts it, or open the studio from the command palette; the run shows up as a live card in the thread. 31 templates, human and dialogue nodes, per-attempt token counts, checkpointed runs. The work templates use Matt Pocock's skills, a separate install (npx skills add mattpocock/skills).

graphite-stack.description: Review stacked changes alongside your BB threads. Inspect parent-relative diffs and keep local comments before sending them to a linked thread. Review GitHub pull requests and preview stack actions. Requires the Graphite CLI; GitHub review features also require an authenticated GitHub CLI.

grok-build-usage.description: Adds live Grok Build subscription and weekly credit usage, including reset timing, to bb's Settings → Usage Limits page.
