gtd-sidebar.description: Replaces the bb thread list with an inbox that splits threads into Next Action and Waiting, and clears them with snooze and settle.

guest-view.description: Share one thread with someone who has no BB account: they follow it live in a browser and suggest prompts that you approve. Guests see your messages and the agent's replies as they happen, with tool work shown only as counts such as "Ran 3 commands, edited 2 files". Each suggestion waits in a card above your composer, where you choose Use, Copy or Dismiss, so nothing a guest writes reaches the agent until you send it. The card also shows who is connected, kicks a guest, ends the link, and sets how long it lasts (4 hours by default). The link is a free Cloudflare quick tunnel, so the thread's text passes through Cloudflare and anyone with the link can watch; it needs the separate cloudflared program (on Linux the plugin can download a pinned, checksummed copy when you ask), and it requires BB 0.48 or later.

guided-review.description: Organizes GitHub pull requests into chapters, with code diffs, private notes, a contextual assistant, and review feedback you edit and submit.

handoff.description: Moves a whole session between agents and machines in both directions: hands a bb thread's rendered transcript to another provider (optionally on another enrolled machine, carrying uncommitted work as a patch), or adopts a Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode session from your terminal as a bb thread in the same directory.

harness.description: Adds an opt-in Explore, Plan, Worker, Critic, and Promote workflow to BB threads with explicit DAGs, role routing, audit artifacts, and custom Harness definitions.

hats.description: Workspaces for your bb sidebar: switch between groups of projects, like Work and Personal, with one click. Each hat is a workspace that holds a set of projects, and a project can sit in several hats. A footer button switches to the next hat: projects that other hats claim are hidden, and projects in no hat always show. Your sidebar order, threads, and collapsed groups stay exactly as you left them. Edit hats and pick their icons on the settings page, or use the bb hats CLI; no account or external service.

haze.description: Puts your own image behind every BB conversation as a soft haze that fades out before the text. Pick one of six effects (None, Dither, ASCII, Halftone, Scanlines, Haze) and set a separate background for each project. Window glass can blur the same image behind the whole window, with a see-through sidebar and main pane. Images stay in your BB server's local database; no account is needed. Turn off Aura while Haze is on.

header-pins.description: Switch between your pinned threads in one click from the empty title bar strip at the top of the BB window. Each chip carries a status dot for the thread and its child threads: yellow waits for you, blue works, green finished and unread. A colored bar marks the thread with its project color when Chat Sidebar by Evgeniy Perin is installed, which we recommend, and with its provider's color otherwise. Hover a chip to unpin it in place. Needs the BB desktop app; no account or network access.

herald.description: Hear one spoken sentence when an agent needs you, and see every waiting thread in one list. When a thread asks a question, waits for a plan or a permission to be approved, finishes its turn or fails, the bb app says which thread it is and what it needs, on whatever page you are on. A Herald page in the sidebar lists every thread waiting on you with its reason and sentence, and the same sentence sits above that thread's composer with a Read again button until you answer. Settings choose which kinds of event are announced, the voice and speed, and where to speak: the desktop app, a browser tab, or the mobile app while it is open. By default the sentence is built from the event itself, with no model or external service; optionally, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI or a command of your own, installed and logged in on the Mac running bb, writes it instead, for one short model turn per announcement. The default voice needs bb running on a Mac, and elsewhere each device's own browser voice speaks. Requires bb 0.47 or later.

herdr-theme.description: Turn BB into a terminal-style workspace, with framed conversation panes and eleven color palettes in light and dark. Child threads hang from their parent as a connected tree in the sidebar. Turn on branch names to show each project thread's Git branch beneath its title. JetBrains Mono ships inside the plugin, so no font service, account, or API key is needed. Requires BB 0.43 or later.

hex.description: On-device voice dictation for BB's chat composer and `bb voice transcribe`, powered by Hex and macOS 26's built-in Apple Speech (SpeechTranscriber + SpeechAnalyzer) or local GGUF speech models (Parakeet, Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, Cohere Transcribe, Nemotron). Starts a warm embedded `hex service --embedded` daemon when BB loads the plugin, adds a Voice Provider picker directly to the composer microphone right-click menu, transcodes browser microphone clips (`audio/webm`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/ogg`) to 16 kHz mono PCM WAV via `ffmpeg`, and stops the daemon automatically when BB exits.

higgsfield.description: Shows how many Higgsfield credits you have, when they reset, and how many will expire unused at your current pace. A burn forecast charts this cycle's balance and projects it to the reset date, so you see whether you run out early or leave credits behind. A per-model table counts generations, refunded failures, credits, and cost per generation, tagged image, video, audio, or text. A daily chart stacks spend by model or media type for this cycle, 7, 30, or 90 days. Requires the Higgsfield CLI and a Higgsfield account; sign-in uses Higgsfield's own browser login.

hmm-floating-terminal.description: Keep a shell open beside the project you are working in, without leaving the conversation for a panel or another app. The window follows the project: leave for another one and it steps aside, come back and its tabs return with the dev server still running. Shells belong to the project checkout rather than to a thread, so moving between a project's threads never costs you one. Sessions belong to BB, so closing the window leaves a build or an ssh session running and reopening replays the scrollback. Drag the grip to resize, minimize to the title bar, or maximize to fill the app. Requires BB 0.42 or newer and Plugin SDK 0.4.47 or newer.

home-hero.description: Greets you on BB's home screen with the time of day and, when you set one, your name. Optionally upload a PNG, JPEG or WebP icon up to 256 KiB; it travels over BB's existing plugin connection and is stored with the plugin on the BB server, never in the repository. Without a name or icon the greeting is plain text. Requires BB 0.49.0+.

homepage.description: Starts new chats from configurable homepage project cards with manual sorting, pinning, renaming, hiding, activity sparklines, and artwork.

hooks.description: Run your own commands and webhooks when BB threads change state, and hold each outgoing message to your own policy. Install notification, integration, automation and guard templates from the marketplace catalog, each rated for performance and security, or write hooks by hand. React to thread lifecycle events with filters on project, provider, title and text; gate hooks proceed, reject with a reason, or wait before dispatch. Secrets stay AES-256-GCM encrypted and are referenced without storing values in hook definitions; manage everything from the Hooks page, `bb hooks`, or the bundled agent skills. Commands run on the machine hosting the BB server with the server user's access.

host-monitor.description: Monitors CPU, memory, disk, network throughput, load, uptime, and user-owned processes across every machine enrolled in bb, with guarded controls to stop eligible processes.

hotspot.description: Names the BB thread that is making your Mac hot, and lets you stop the dev server or build behind it. A flame in the sidebar footer shows CPU and memory every 2 seconds; click it for the busiest threads, each thread's processes, and a kill that lists what it stops and what it spares before it runs. The Hotspot page keeps seven days of per-minute CPU, memory and thermal history, shades each hot spell, and ranks the threads that caused it. Agents answer "why was my Mac hot at 3pm?" with a built-in tool, and the bb hotspot command answers it in a terminal. Built for macOS, with no account or network service; on Linux it tracks CPU, memory and threads but has no thermal reading, and Windows is not supported.

human-tasks.description: Collect the steps only you can do in one checklist, and the agent that asked resumes when you finish. Agents hand you tasks with steps, like creating an API key, adding a DNS record, or testing a build on your phone, each linked to the project, thread, and bot that asked. Each task says what the agent would need to do it itself, such as an MCP server, an API key, or your browser, so you can do it or let the agent do it. Blocking tasks wait as a form in their thread so your push notifications fire, and credentials come back through bb's secret form instead of the chat.

image-diff.description: See exactly which pixels changed in an image before you approve it. Before, Diff and After sit side by side, with changed pixels highlighted over a white background, over the new image, or blinking, plus a changed-pixel count. Git LFS images render in place in BB's Diff tab, downloading missing objects on demand. A pinned Image diff tab lists every changed image in the thread, and opening a changed image anywhere shows its diff. LFS images need git-lfs on the host.

image-studio.description: Keep generated project photos in a gallery and create or edit the next image from the panel or chat. People profiles use labeled reference sheets and can build missing face, body, and detail views for reuse across models. Nano Banana 2, 2.1, Pro, and Muse Image use paid fal.ai or kie.ai API keys; Muse Image requires fal.ai. The chat Send form remembers the model, frame, and size, with 2K as the default size; the interface supports English and Russian, and Env Catalog can hold the keys.

inbox.description: Questions, failed runs, finished threads, and extension activity in one inbox, with dismissible popups, optional Telegram alerts, and guided setup.

inline-comments.description: Comment on exact passages of an agent's reply and send every comment with your next message. Select text, choose Add to chat, and type or dictate a note in a card next to the passage. Each passage stays highlighted and appears as a pill in the composer, where a click edits or deletes its comment. The agent receives each quoted passage next to its comment. Comments stay on your bb server; no external service or account is needed. Requires bb 0.46 or later.

inline-review.description: Turn passages from an assistant response into one clear revision request. Mark comments and removals while you read, keep them highlighted across navigation, add overall feedback, and send the full review to the same thread. Drafts stay on your BB server; no external service or account is required. Requires BB 0.43.x.

ios-simulator.description: Run and test mobile apps beside your BB thread, using the same screen as your agent. Capture up to the last 30 seconds of iOS video with input, app-log, and matching crash events. Hand control explicitly between you and your agent, with one controlling thread per device. Requires BB 0.46+, an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode’s iOS platform and Node.js 20+ for iOS; Android screenshot previews need an installed SDK and AVD.

iris.description: Turns agent replies into live cards you can use: charts, test runs, decisions, plans, agent traces, eval reports and small apps, drawn in your bb theme. Agents pick from well over a hundred components on their own and check each card before you see it, so a status report arrives as metrics and progress, and proof of done as criteria with their evidence. Sliders and toggles recompute cards in place, buttons and pickers send your answer back to the agent (design variants, a theme preview, colors, marks on a screenshot, comments on a spec, a ranked list), and live cards re-read files while a job runs. Pin up to five live cards per thread, or let the agent pin a status card: a pinned chip above the composer opens them, bb's home page shows every thread's pins, and a pin can alert you when its condition turns true. Copy any card as an image, or open it in the web playground. Cards also read bb itself: the thread's context use, the threads it started, its pull request, commits, terminals and plan usage. Adds under 4,000 tokens of instructions to each top-level session, and maps and photos call OpenStreetMap, Photon and Wikimedia Commons unless you turn web lookups off.

jb-flow.description: Puts the agent threads that need you at the top, and keeps the rest out of the way until they do. A Triage sidebar ranks what to do next in Now: what's blocked on you, threads you mark as Focus, and deadlines coming up, above numbered lanes you move between with one key. Workspace tabs group projects, threads and tools by area of work. ⌘K searches threads, messages and PRs, and Tab on a result replies to it, snoozes, moves or archives it. Agents call wait_for_ci and end their turn instead of polling GitHub, and are messaged when checks finish or a review arrives. PR and CI features need the GitHub CLI.

jetbrains-central.description: Use work AI subscriptions alongside personal accounts and see shared JetBrains Central credits in BB. This is an unofficial plugin developed independently by an enthusiast. It is not an official JetBrains product. JetBrains Air is JetBrains' platform for coding agents and team AI access; this plugin connects BB through JetBrains Central CLI using your JetBrains Account. Choose separate Codex, Claude Code, and Pi providers, or configure additional ACP profiles. Requires BB 0.48+ with Plugin SDK 0.6.104+, Git, Node.js, Central with a work subscription or organization-provided AI access, and the corresponding agent CLIs; tested on macOS.

jev-please-proceed.description: Keep agents moving when they stop only to ask for an unnecessary confirmation. Jev reviews the complete available top-level conversation whenever a thread becomes idle and continues only when its Noul value exceeds 0.95. Before sending `please proceed`, it confirms that the thread is still idle and has no pending interaction or queued message, then stops if the same final response repeats. Use a TypeSafe, Vercel AI Gateway, or OpenRouter API key; conversation text is sent through the selected provider for TypeSafe processing, and usage charges may apply.

jira.description: Browse, edit, and move Jira Cloud issues without leaving BB, and let agents change Jira only after you approve. Switch between a grouped list and a status board, and drag a card to move an issue through its workflow. Agents can search, create, edit, transition, comment on, assign, and delete issues, and each kind of change asks first unless you set it to always allow. Link a BB project to its Jira projects so that project's chats search only those issues, and Send to agent opens the chat in the linked project. Requires a Jira Cloud site and an Atlassian API token; Jira Server and Data Center are not supported.

jira-boards.description: Browse your Jira boards beside the chat and add any ticket's current context to your next message. Columns, quick filters, JQL and swimlanes by assignee, epic or priority keep the board to the work you care about, and the tab reopens on your last board and filters. Drag a card into the composer or press Add to chat, and BB fetches the issue, its fields and newest comments when you send. Agents can read issues, individual fields, comment pages, text attachments such as logs and JSON, and linked issues and subtasks in one call, and post a comment, move a ticket through its workflow or assign it to you when you ask, as your own Jira account. Works with Jira Data Center or Server through a personal access token and with Jira Cloud through an API token plus account email; the BB server needs HTTPS access to the Jira site. Needs BB 0.47 or newer.

jira-dc.description: Browse and update Jira Data Center issues from BB, and let agents change them only after you approve. Open a list or status board, edit fields in place, and drag a card through the workflow. Agents can search, create, edit, transition, comment on, assign, and delete issues, with each write kind asking first unless you set it to always allow. Link a BB project to its Jira projects so chats stay scoped, spawn a thread from an issue, or drive the same actions with bb jira-dc. Requires a reachable Jira Data Center (or Server) base URL and a Personal Access Token; Jira Cloud is not supported.

kata.description: Track and triage kata issues from the keyboard, beside the bb thread doing the work. One tab per kata project puts the issue list and the issue detail side by side, updated live from the kata daemon. Press n for a new issue inline, N for a child of the selection, and !0-!4 to set priority without leaving the list. A thread whose checkout holds a .kata.toml gets a Kata issues side panel, clickable issue chips in messages, and kata_* tools its agent can call. The bb kata CLI covers the same ground from any bb terminal. Requires kata installed on the same machine with its daemon running; no account, token, or hosted service.

keep-last-blocks-open.description: Keeps the newest work blocks open while the agent works, so the output stays in view without clicks. Blocks count at every depth, so the commands inside a group count toward the limit. After the final answer only the last block stays open. Settings set the running count from 0 to 10, the count after the answer from 0 to 3, and whether Thought rows count. Needs no account or external service.

kernel-browser.description: Open, watch, and drive KERNEL cloud browsers from bb threads and the bb CLI.

kilocode.description: First-class Kilo Code provider for BB.

kimi-code.description: Adds Moonshot's Kimi Code as a provider: run its threads from bb's provider picker, locally and on enrolled remote hosts. Turns stream into the native bb timeline — replies and tool calls such as file edits and shell commands — with resume and bb permission modes gating each action. The model picker fills from Kimi Code itself (K3, K3-256k, K2.8 Preview, K2.7 Code Highspeed), with thinking levels and the Default / Plan / Auto / YOLO mode selector. Kimi Code's slash commands (/compact, /status, /usage, and your own skill commands) appear in the composer menu. Requires the Kimi Code CLI and a signed-in account on each host (kimi login); the provider card can install the CLI where it is missing.

kimi-quota.description: See Kimi Code quota beside Codex and Claude limits in one BB usage card. Shows the 5-hour window, monthly coding and total limits, with reset times; also provides the bb kimi-quota command. Uses Kimi's API and requires Kimi Code CLI installed and signed in on the BB server, plus a Kimi membership that includes Kimi Code.

kimi-usage.description: Shows the Kimi Code 5-hour and monthly limits in bb's usage panel, where no collector reads them. The panel covers the OpenCode Go and Claude Code subscriptions only, so a Kimi Code plan shows nothing; this adds the windows Kimi reports, with the percentage used and the reset time. The row appears only when the Kimi Code ACP provider is installed, and a host whose login expired drops out instead of leaving an empty row. Requires a Kimi Code subscription signed in on the host.

kodaforge.description: Edit, run and debug your project inside BB, with agent chat, threads and workflows open beside the code. A Monaco code editor with tabs, split editors, quick open (⌘P), find in files, and search and replace with a preview. Language servers (LSP) for Python and TypeScript give completion, go to definition, find references, rename and a Problems panel. Debug Python with breakpoints, pick the Python environment (venv, uv, Poetry, conda), run Makefile and npm tasks, and work in split terminals that survive restarts. Source control stages, diffs, commits, stashes, pulls and pushes with git. The Agent Network maps the agents and MCP servers working on your project, and in App mode the agents, tools, MCP servers, models and skills your code builds. Install the language servers (pyright or basedpyright, typescript-language-server) and debugpy yourself.

korey.description: Bring all your Korey connectors into your coding conversations in bb. Research across connected services and create or update Shortcut Stories. Continue the same private Korey conversation across coding harnesses and attach workspace files. Requires a Korey account, a personal access token, and configured connectors.

lame-duck.description: Make a busy BB server ready for maintenance while keeping new sends queued. Pause sends while active turns finish, and watch the active-thread and held-send counts in the sidebar. Resume queued work after the server restarts. Agents can manage the same flow through the bb CLI.

launchd-jobs.description: Run shell commands on your Mac on a cron schedule or a fixed interval, as launchd jobs that keep running while bb is closed. Each job is a LaunchAgent plist that launchd owns, so a missed fire runs once when the Mac wakes and a disabled job stays disabled across reboots. A sidebar page shows each job's launchd status, its last twenty runs with duration and exit code, and the tail of its log, which you can follow live. Run now, Enable, Disable, Edit and Delete do the launchctl work for you, and commands run through your login shell with your terminal's PATH. The sidebar row counts failing jobs, and a picker switches between the Macs connected to bb. An optional push notification tells you when a job starts failing, once per failure; it needs bb 0.48.1 or later with Push notifications on. Requires bb 0.47 or later and macOS.

lavender.description: Give your workspace a lavender palette, from charcoal-violet nights to pale-lilac days. Match conversations, menus, code previews and diffs with coordinated light and dark colors. Follow your Light, Dark or System setting while keeping your layout and fonts. All theme assets ship locally; no external account is required.

learning-exercises.description: Get a short exercise on the code your agents just wrote, so you keep understanding what lands in your repository. After a commit, new files, a schema change or a merged pull request, one line above the composer offers a 10–15 minute exercise; offers are decided from bb's own data, not by a model, and are capped at three answered a day. Start runs the session in a side thread forked from yours, where each question is a card for your answer and how sure you are, and the agent's turn ends while the card is open, so it cannot hint. A Learning tab in every thread's side panel shows the session in progress, starts an exercise on the last commit, the new files or a topic you type, and keeps the project's paused and earlier sessions with your answers. A session runs on the thread's own agent and uses its tokens; answers are stored on the machine running bb. Exercises adapted from Dr. Cat Hicks's Learning Opportunities (CC BY 4.0), not affiliated with or endorsed by the author. Requires bb 0.48.1 or later with bb's bundled Git plugin on; pull request offers also need GitHub PR Status.

lego.description: Split a coding task across parallel agents and get it back assembled and verified by one Master Builder, while a Lego model builds live. The planning agent writes an instruction book: bags that each own their files, the interfaces every bag must honour, and the steps to assemble them. You choose how many builders run, up to eight, and which provider and model the builders and the Master Builder use; nothing starts until you submit. A banner above the composer and a side-panel workbench show minifigure builders placing bricks as each step lands, and finished models go on a collector's shelf. Builders and the Master Builder are ordinary BB threads on providers you already set up, so a build spends several agents' worth of tokens.

letta-agents.description: Resume your local Letta agents from the sidebar without losing their saved conversations. See agent activity and dispatched tasks beside each agent. Keep agent providers out of the model picker unless you enable them. Requires a separate local Letta Docker installation with the supported filesystem layout, Docker access, and the BB ACP adapter; the adapter uses npx to install its pinned Letta ACP package.

linear.description: Linear inside bb — a list-first issue browser, inbox, and create dialog served from a local mirror, thirteen linear_* agent tools, a bb linear CLI, and every thread resolving which issue it works on, shown live in the header and side panel and injected into agent context.

linear-card.description: See which Linear issue each chat is about, right in the thread header. Click the chip for the full card with its description and images, then open, change, or unlink it. A chat with no card opens your assigned issues, grouped by state and searchable, so you can link one in two clicks. Branches named by Linear (eng-123-…) attach their issue on their own, and long titles get a short AI label. Requires a Linear personal API key; short labels use bb's Account Pooler.

link-hovercards.description: See a pull request's CI, review and merge state by hovering its link, without leaving the thread. Works on GitHub pull requests, GitHub issues and Linear issues anywhere in BB. On a phone, long-press a link to open its card. GitHub cards need the GitHub CLI signed in on your BB server; Linear cards need a personal Linear API key.

liquid-glass.description: Adds dark and light translucent themes over a configurable wallpaper layer, with adjustable glass effects and vibrant accent colors.

live-markdown.description: Edit Markdown right in the side panel, with formatting rendered as you type and saves that change only the characters you typed. Tables stay tables while you edit: click a cell to change its raw Markdown in place, Tab to the next cell, and Tab past the last one to add a row. Every save checks the file's hash first, so a file an agent changed while you typed asks you to keep your version or load the disk version instead of being overwritten. It becomes the opener for .md, .mdx and .markdown files on install unless you already chose one under Settings, and needs bb 0.43 or later with no account or external service.

lobu.description: Starts every thread with what earlier threads learned in your project and saves new learnings to Lobu memory. Agents search your personal workspace and a linked team workspace before working, supersede outdated memories in place, and run through native tools or bb lobu CLI commands across every agent provider. Each thread's Lobu memory panel shows what the agent started with, looked up, and saved, with undo, project pins, and one-click sharing to your team workspace. A Lobu page in bb's sidebar shows what agents saved in bb threads, searches all of Lobu, and surfaces the inbox plus the devices and connections that need attention. Built-in setup on the New thread screen installs the Lobu CLI via bun or npm and connects to a Lobu Cloud account or a local Lobu instance running on your machine.

lock-area.description: Keep reference panes in place while opening work beside them. Uses compatible native locks, or offers a version-checked initializer with backup and restore for BB 0.43.1. Initialization requires a clean supported BB source checkout, installed dependencies and pnpm.

loom.description: Hand a goal to agents and keep the decisions. A planner turns it into a spec with tickets, acceptance criteria, checks and a merge plan, and a separate agent reviews the spec before you approve it. Workers then build each ticket in its own git worktree, Loom runs your checks, and reviewers on another model approve the work or send findings back. Approved work merges into an integration branch you land as one pull request, or opens as one pull request per ticket that Loom follows through CI. A full-screen Loom page shows what needs you, the board, every attempt and review, the changes before they land, insights on how the project went and a timeline you can rewind.

mac-watch.description: Watch the Mac that runs bb — battery, heat, disk and sleep — from your phone. A macOS-style sidebar page shows CPU, memory pressure, disk, network and power draw with 1, 6 and 24 hour charts, plus the apps that hold the machine awake. Processor, SSD and battery temperatures, macOS thermal pressure, SMART status and kernel panics are read without sudo. Pushes cover only real trouble: battery under 20%, overheating, memory or disk running out, battery-controller faults and an unexpected reboot, with warnings held until morning during quiet hours. macOS on Apple Silicon only; alerts need the push-notifications plugin, sleep and shutdown add a one-time sudoers rule, and the interface is in Russian.

machine-load.description: Compare CPU, memory, GPU, network and disk load of all your bb machines on one shared timeline, with up to 7 days of history. Each machine gets a card with load average, swap, disk usage, disk IO, CPU temperature and every GPU, including Intel integrated graphics and Apple silicon, read without root. Agents check load before a heavy job with bb machine-load --json. A sidebar badge appears when any machine passes 80% CPU or RAM. Apple silicon temperature and power need macmon, installed separately.

machine-sidebar.description: Sort your bb threads by the machine they run on, then by project, so laptop and remote work never mix. Mark quiet threads or whole projects inactive to fold them into a dimmed group at the bottom; they come back when a turn finishes or waits for you. Start a title with [Tag] to show a colored pill, with a color per tag you pick in the plugin settings. Each row shows its git branch, a status dot, and icons for subagents or background commands; with farcall-mcp, worker tasks appear under their coordinator, each with the worktree it runs in.

machine-status.description: See battery charge, memory use, and disk use for every machine connected to bb in one sidebar list. Each metric turns red at a threshold you set — 20% battery, 90% memory or storage by default. The list refreshes only when a whole-percent value changes, so it stays still while you work. Turn off the metrics you do not need; everything comes from each machine's own OS interfaces, with no account or external service.

magic-compose.description: Choose where a new thread runs as you type your prompt. Let Jev select the project, machine, model, reasoning level, and environment, then review or override each choice before sending. Tune its choices with your instructions and try routing a prompt from settings. Requires BB 0.43+ and a Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter API key; prompts, routing instructions, project context, and machine information are sent to TypeSafe through your gateway, with usage charges.

magpie.description: Connect BB to a Magpie gateway and see what your agents cost. The Magpie page shows estimated cost, tokens over time per agent, cache hit rate, subscription allowance with reset times, and a breakdown by model, agent, or day. Sync models puts Magpie models into the Pi, Codex, and Claude Code pickers, and you can route one thread or a whole provider through Magpie. Gateway keys stay on the BB server.

mane-control.description: Switch Ponytail between Off, Lite, Full, and Ultra in one click, so how hard the agent works matches the task in front of you. A horse button beside the thread composer lists the four modes with a line on what each one does, and keeps the active mode in view. Picking a mode sends the /ponytail command for you, and those commands collapse into compact status pills in the transcript instead of stray slash-command lines. Needs the Ponytail skill installed for the thread's provider, and the control stays disabled until it finds one.
