matt-pocock-skills-for-bb.description: Gives your agents Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity skills as slash commands, from test-first development to issue triage. Choose which skills each project gets, or turn them on only in the projects you pick; Matt's 6 experimental skills stay off until you opt in. A skill you already have keeps its name, and you can keep both, with Matt's as matt-pocock-<name>. Turning off a skill that another one needs asks first and names what else changes. New releases follow mattpocock/skills daily; some skills use Git or GitHub CLI, and no account is needed.

md-editor.description: Edit agent-written Markdown as a formatted document, and send any passage to the chat with its file path and line numbers. Callouts, collapsible details, footnotes, raw HTML and YAML properties render in place and save back unchanged, so opening a file never rewrites it. Mermaid flowcharts are edited by right-click (add a block or a yes/no branch, change a shape, delete), and LaTeX, code highlighting for 37 languages and directory trees render alongside. Files open from the machine and folder of the thread they came from, and autosave stops instead of overwriting a change an agent made underneath you. Adds a markdown-pro agent skill and a close-others and pin menu on the side-panel tabs; needs BB 0.43 or later and no account or external service.

md-prompt.description: Read Markdown and code with live formatting as you write your prompt. Code fences gain syntax colours before you close them. Toggle highlighting in the composer, settings or CLI without changing the text sent to your agent. Requires BB 0.47 or later; no external service, account or API key.

media-viewer.description: Zoom into screenshots, step through recordings and play audio in bb's right panel instead of a fit-only preview. Drag to pan, pinch or Ctrl-scroll to zoom at the pointer, and double-click to switch between Fit and a close-up. Previous and next step through every image, video and audio file in the same folder. Videos get frame stepping, seeking and speeds from 0.25× to 2×, and agents can show the same viewer inline in a reply with a ::media directive.

meetings.description: Keep recordings, transcripts and action items from Zoom, Google Meet, Telemost and Jitsi calls together. Record and transcribe Russian speech on a Linux x64 or arm64 host with Chrome, Xvfb, PulseAudio, ffmpeg and the separately installed GigaAM plugin or your own transcription server. Use five built-in or custom summary templates, transcript search, timecoded Q&A, optional calendar auto-join and external agents through MCP or REST. A BB agent or an optional model API writes summaries; calendar sync needs Google OAuth or an ICS feed, and admission can require a platform account.

memory-explorer.description: See what your agents remember: BB memory as a searchable table and a zoomable link graph, with a detail drawer for each memory. Search and filter every global and project memory, follow the links between memories, and see what links back to each one. Confirm or discard the preferences agents marked unconfirmed, and keep your own notes on people, teams and initiatives. Needs BB 0.48 or later and BB's Memory plugin.

message-date-time.description: Puts the date and time above every message in a thread, yours and the agent's. Labels read "Today, 2:34 PM", "Yesterday, 22:10" or "Oct 3, 9:15 AM", and older messages add the year. Choose English or Russian and a 12- or 24-hour clock, or let the plugin follow your computer's settings. A BB update can hide the labels until the plugin catches up; the chat keeps working.

miku.description: Keep Hatsune Miku beside you while you work, with a roaming pixel-art companion that reacts to activity across BB. Drag her out of the way, keep her in place, or hide her from the command palette. Enable agent-powered comments using a configured BB provider and its account or usage allowance. Optional synthesized voice runs locally and requires FFmpeg with Flite and Rubber Band on the BB server.

millivolt.description: See every AI request your agents make, and what it cost, without leaving bb. The plugin installs millivolt for you or adopts a deployment you already run, then keeps it current on each bb start. Its sidebar shows live requests, tokens, cost and latency next to the full millivolt dashboard for settings, holds and debugging. Needs Docker; millivolt keeps its own SQLite history in a Docker volume and listens on loopback only.

minimap.description: A scrollbar you can read: a strip along the right edge of each thread, drawn like VS Code's minimap, with one rectangle per message, as tall as the message and coloured by kind (your messages, agent replies, work, errors, system notes). Drag its slider to scrub, click to glide there, scroll the wheel over it, or hover to see the rows around the pointer with an icon and the start of each one's text. It replaces BB's fading scrollbar, or keeps it beside the strip, casts a soft shade on a dark theme, and a settings panel in the thread menu sets the size, colours, slider, note and scrolling while you watch. It reads only what changed while a turn works and nothing while the strip is not shown. Requires BB 0.49 or later.

minus.description: Hide the bb controls you never click and fold runs of tool calls into one "Called N tools" row. Twenty-seven switches in Settings, grouped by area, each remove one element: back/forward buttons, sidebar and panel toggles, "..." menus, the Commit and "Open in" buttons, the prompt box buttons and the items under it, the message navigator, message and code block hover buttons, thinking rows, thread provider icons, and the macOS workbench padding. Changes apply in every open window without a reload, and keyboard shortcuts keep working for hidden controls. A bb update that renames an element can bring it back until the plugin catches up.

moa.description: Compare two independent perspectives before your chat model acts on each request. Enable MoA per chat, share model and fallback settings across chats, and inspect each participant’s input, answer and delivery receipt from the message history. Advisors retain separate sessions, and active models can continue beyond a long-wait notice. Uses your configured BB providers and accounts, adding model calls, latency and provider usage; remote file reads require the separately installed File Gateway plugin.

moa-provider.description: Get a second and third opinion on every message before one agent changes your files. Each preset you build becomes a model in the model picker: up to six advisor models answer in parallel, then an aggregator model reads their notes and does the work. A live panel in the thread shows what each advisor is doing and its answer as it streams. Type /moa in any other thread to put a question to the same advisors, or have the aggregator check in with them every few tool calls. Uses the providers you already installed and signed in to; each advisor adds a model turn to every message, and what an advisor reads goes to its model's provider.

model-effort-badges.description: See each thread’s model and reasoning effort in the BB sidebar. Hover for the full name.

model-favicons.description: Gives every agent its own logo, so custom ACP agents stop sharing one generic icon. Pick a mark per provider from the sidebar or the bb model-favicons command, and nine bundled marks cover GLM, Kimi, MiniMax Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Claude, Codex, and Gemini. Applies in the model picker and every provider list, in light and dark. Needs BB 0.49 or newer and a configured ACP provider.

model-presets.description: Adds a preset menu to the New thread composer that sets provider, model, effort, and speed in one step, applies custom instructions to threads started with it, and opens by keyboard shortcut with number keys to pick.

model-pricing.description: Compare what every AI model costs per million tokens, across Anthropic, OpenAI, Fireworks AI, Ollama Cloud and OpenRouter, in one table. A Relative column ranks each model against the cheapest one on screen, weighted by an input/output blend you choose. Each row also gives the context window, the longest reply, and whether the model can reason, call tools or return structured output. Sort by any column, search by name, hide a provider with its legend dot, and open any model's own page from its row. Prices come from the public models.dev catalog and OpenRouter's model list and are kept for twelve hours; no account or key is needed, but the machine running the bb server must reach both sites.

model-visibility.description: Keep the model picker short without losing access to any model. Move chosen model IDs out of the main list and into More models, where they stay selectable and searchable. Hide models per provider, with Hide all for a whole catalog and a Configure... shortcut in More models. Hiding is display-only: the selected model, reasoning level, service tier, and provider catalogs are unchanged. Experimental and desktop-only for BB 0.47.1; the compact picker fails open, and a future picker layout change may need a plugin update.

monokai.description: A dark Monokai-family theme for bb: one meaning per hue, a single text ladder, and a matching terminal palette.

multi-repo-git.description: Keep related projects and conversations within reach without replacing BB's native workspace tree. Group subprojects into workspaces and page each project's chat families (1–100, default 5). Recent loads chats 50 at a time as you scroll and searches titles and project names across all visible, non-archived chats with saved messages. Work and unread status remain visible together, including activity in child chats. Includes repository-local Source Control; requires BB 0.48.1+, SDK 0.6.104+, Node 24.20.0+ and the built-in thread-list, with no external service or paid account.

my-jira.description: See every Jira ticket assigned to you in one bb tab, filtered and grouped the way you work, and move it along without opening Jira. Filter by status and type, search by key or words, and group by status, initiative and epic, or the boards that list each ticket. Open a ticket beside the list to read its lineage, description, subtasks and comments, then step to the next one with Previous and Next or the keyboard. Change a status in place from the moves your workflow allows. Needs Jira Cloud with Atlassian's Rovo MCP server allowed for your organization; you sign in with Atlassian in the browser and set up nothing else.

my-tasks.description: Plan personal work with sections, nested steps and optional agent assistance. Review suggestions before accepting them. Assistance requires an authenticated Codex CLI and uses provider quota.

nanogpt-provider.description: Run bb threads on NanoGPT's models, unlocked by your own API key. Paste the key into a gear in the composer; NanoGPT checks it before bb stores it, and a rejected key unlocks no models. Answers stream in with a separate reasoning channel, and the agent can call bb's tools in your project. Needs a NanoGPT account and API key, and NanoGPT bills your usage.

nav-rail.description: Make more room for threads with a vertical strip of sidebar icons. Keep your saved navigation order and hidden destinations, with controls to rearrange them or open panels in a split. Start a new thread from the sidebar header, and use hover labels, selected states, and badges to find your way. Requires BB 0.42+ and Plugin SDK 0.5.15+, with no extra service, account, or API key.

next-prompt.description: Shows up to three prompts you are likely to type next after each finished turn, one key from your draft. Click a card, or press Tab or → in the empty composer, to put it in your draft; nothing is sent unless you set clicks to send. Show them as numbered cards above the composer, as grey text inside it, or both. Choose the model with bb's provider and model picker: Claude Code and Codex models run as one CLI call with no tools, and any other provider runs as a hidden worker thread. Only the thread's user and assistant messages are sent, never tool output, and hidden and child threads are skipped. Each suggestion request runs on a provider you already use; the default, Claude Sonnet 5.5, needs the claude CLI signed in on the bb server.

next-step.description: Turn a finished Codex answer into an editable next request. Accept one suggestion with Tab or a tap, then edit and send it yourself. Dismiss it with Esc; existing drafts and attachments stay intact. Requires BB 0.49+ and an installed, signed-in Codex CLI; each generated suggestion uses additional Codex quota.

noted.description: Point at the exact part of an agent's HTML or Markdown artifact and send that feedback straight to its thread. Click an element or select text in the side panel, type a note, and queue as many notes as you want before sending them as one message. Each note reaches the agent with the element's selector and the quoted text, so it edits the right spot instead of guessing which paragraph you meant. When the agent saves the file, the open review refreshes to the next revision. Optional settings add a separate review window and in-place Markdown source editing.

notify.description: Sends a native macOS notification when a bb thread finishes or fails, and adds a notify_user agent tool plus a bb notify command.

notify-feed.description: Keep your conversation from drowning in child-thread reports when a thread delegates work. Background messages and completion notices move to a Notifications tab beside the feed. Browse updates by thread or day, and reply directly from the panel. Works inside BB with no external service.

notion-theme.description: Give BB Notion's page colours and type in light and dark, then pick Default, Serif or Mono for messages. Menus, dialogs, switches and your own bubble follow those shapes; markdown in the thread uses Notion's inline code, quotes, headings and tables. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, and a click pins them. A notice on the prompt box appears when a provider window is exhausted and can retry at reset. No account; licensed Notion fonts are named first, then system fallbacks.

now-playing.description: Play, pause, and skip tracks from a small player in the bb sidebar footer. The player shows the current track with album art, a seek bar, shuffle, repeat, and volume, in one of seven styles: Default, Minimal, Cover, Hi-Fi, Terminal, Pocket, and the bb-amp skin. The styles follow your bb theme in light and dark mode, and four of them take an accent color. It controls the music player on the computer that runs the bb server: Spotify or Apple Music on macOS, and any MPRIS player on Linux (needs playerctl) or any app in the media overlay on Windows (no volume control there). By default the player follows the app that is playing, and a setting locks it to Spotify or Apple Music. The bb music command gives terminals and agents the same controls. On macOS, Spotify needs its desktop app, and macOS asks once for permission to control each app. Covers for streamed Apple Music tracks come from Apple's iTunes Search API, which receives the artist and title; a setting turns this off.

nudge.description: Continue or retry the agent from an empty composer. Play replaces Send while the draft is empty, starts idle threads without a user bubble, and retries failed turns by reference. Hidden while the agent is running. Also available as bb nudge. No account or API key.

nudger.description: Agents stop halfway and wait for you to type “go on”. Nudger types it for you: Jev reads each stopped thread and nudges only unfinished work, never past a blocker or a request for permission. Bring your own Jev API key.

ocean-dark.description: Give BB blue-grey surfaces, sky-blue accents and teal highlights. Matching syntax and terminal palettes keep code previews and diffs coordinated. Adapts T3 Code's Ocean dark palette and stays dark in Light, Dark or System mode. Requires BB 0.47.1 or later and a compatible Plugin SDK; no account or external service is needed.

office-viewer.description: Opens Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, images and video right in BB's side panel, on any device you browse from. Spreadsheets recalculate live formulas and save edits to .xlsx and .csv without touching the formatting. Pictures open in an editor for arrows, boxes, text, numbered steps, blur and crop, and the result goes straight into the chat. Select cells, a PDF passage or a slide and quote it to the agent. Runs locally: no account, API key or external service.

ollama-fleet.description: Route local inference across your Ollama servers and see which model handled each job. Inspect health and model inventory, with bounded fallback and job history. Requires BB and a reachable Ollama server; Agent Board 0.6.0 or newer is an optional companion.

ollama-usage.description: Shows what is left in the Ollama Cloud monthly credit pool, with its reset date and the money already spent, in bb's usage panel. The panel reads only the OpenCode Go and Claude Code subscriptions, so an Ollama Cloud plan has no row there; this adds the pool as a dollar window beside them. Spend for the last day, week or month comes with a per-model breakdown, and bb ollama-usage prints the same numbers in a terminal. Needs an Ollama Cloud account with an API key on the host, either OLLAMA_API_KEY or the sign-in OpenCode already stored.

omarchy.description: Keeps BB desktop and PWA colors in step with the active Omarchy theme, including light/dark mode, ANSI and code colors, favicon tinting, and animated transitions, while leaving the native mobile app independent.

omp-subagents.description: Watch OMP subagents work instead of staring at a "Ran tool" row. Each spawn gets a live line per agent under it in the dialog, and the thread header opens a panel with every agent's status, model, tokens, cost, transcript and final output. A box in the panel messages the OMP session, and a bb omp-subagents command gives agents the same view. Requires threads on the omp provider and the omp CLI on the machine that runs them.

open-in-window.description: Opens any thread in its own browser tab or window from the thread's "..." menu, so two threads can stay open side by side. Adds Open in new window to the sidebar row's menu, its right-click menu, and the thread header's menu. Opens the same link Copy link copies, exactly as a target="_blank" link would, so your browser's own tab and window settings decide where it lands. Nothing to configure, no commands, and no network access.

opencode2.description: Run BB threads on any model you've connected to OpenCode v2, with BB's rewind, fork, steering, and permission modes intact. Tool calls show as native BB rows, including live command output and file changes built from OpenCode's own patches. BB dynamic tools, skills, and the bb CLI work inside OpenCode sessions. Needs OpenCode v2 (2.0.26 or newer, installed as opencode2) on the host and a model provider connected with opencode2 auth login.

openrouter-inference.description: Choose the OpenRouter model that writes your thread titles and commit messages. Search models by name or ID, compare token prices and context sizes, and test a sample title before switching. Change the selected model from settings whenever you want. Requires an OpenRouter API key; prompts, thread text, and diffs go to OpenRouter and the selected model provider, with charges billed to your account.

openspec.description: Browse OpenSpec changes and specifications, track task progress, and launch linked agents.

openspec-review.description: Comment on quoted text in OpenSpec proposals, designs and specs, and send the comments to the agent in the chat.

openui.description: Turns agent replies into dashboards, reports, plans and forms you can read at a glance and click, right in the chat. Agents write OpenUI Lang, and the plugin draws it with OpenUI's React component library plus about 70 components of its own: gauges, heatmaps, timelines, roadmaps, kanban boards, test and coverage reports, diffs and maps. Plans, decisions, choices, quizzes and forms send your answer back into the thread as your next message. Components for BB show the thread's changed files, commits, pull request and other threads live. Adds about 3,000 tokens of instructions to sessions whose replies you read, and Map and ImageSearch fetch from OpenStreetMap, Photon, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons unless you turn web lookups off.

operator-inbox.description: Adds a project-scoped inbox where BB agents leave durable messages and operators reply through native threads.

orchestrator-mode.description: Keep one thread as the planner and send every unit of work to its own worker thread. A watchdog checks new timeline work at the guard and block levels, records direct work the parent did itself, and sends up to three corrective messages or stops the turn. Toggle a thread from the composer, its + menu or `bb orchestrator-mode`, and switch the mode on for every new thread you start. Workers share the parent's environment and provider, so they need no extra service; requires bb 0.44 or newer.

otel.description: Send per-turn token, cost and quota data from bb to the OpenTelemetry collector you already run. Each finished turn becomes a span with the model, input, output and cache tokens, and cost when the provider reports it; child threads join the trace of their root thread. Histograms and counters track token usage, turn duration, cost, turns and thread transitions, and gauges follow provider quota windows (used percent, reset time). Prompts, replies, tool text, thread titles, file paths and error messages are never exported, and no setting turns that on. Needs an OpenTelemetry collector that you run; nothing is sent until you set its OTLP/HTTP endpoint.

pad.description: Keep notes beside your work in a local Markdown outline, with keyboard editing and optional agent reviews. Capture notes from the panel, the `bb pad add` command, or the `pad_add` agent tool. Notes stay on your bb server with local Git history; optional reviews send pending notes to your chosen agent provider and use its normal quota or billing. Requires bb 0.49.0 or later and Git.

pets.description: Adds a pixel companion to the BB window that mirrors your fleet, walks to threads waiting on you, and earns XP from finished turns.

pi-command-sync.description: Run Pi's own slash commands inside a BB thread instead of paying a model turn for them. The composer menu lists every command the Pi session has loaded, including extension and prompt commands BB cannot see on its own. /session, /thinking, /model, /name and /reload answer from the addon with no model request, and terminal-only controls such as /login or /resume explain the limitation instead of falling through to the model. Needs a one-time patch to BB's installed Pi provider bundle, applied with the checked script in the repository, because BB 0.45.0 has no API for this. Linux hosts only; macOS is untested and Windows is refused.

pinch-zoom.description: Resize bb's chat, composer and terminal text with a pinch, or switch a setting to scale the whole app. Text scales from 75% to 200%; settings make the composer and terminal half to double the chat size, and terminals re-wrap to their new width when you let go. A pinch over a terminal fine-tunes it on that device. Works with a touchscreen, a trackpad pinch, or Ctrl and the mouse wheel, and a Settings section has A−, A+ and Reset buttons. Terminal sizing and chat-only scaling hook into bb's internal components, so a bb update can break them until the plugin catches up; whole-app text sizing does not depend on them.

pinned-turns.description: Keep the question you are reading under and the agent's last answer in view while you scroll a long thread. Click either one to jump back to it; the page's address and the back button stay as they were. A counter such as 7/23 shows which turn you are on, and a turn that is still running pulses. A Pinned turns submenu in the thread's actions menu switches the bar and each option on or off. It reads BB's timeline layout, which is not a documented interface, so a BB update may need a plugin update. Requires BB 0.48 or later.

plain-paste.description: Pastes only the text of the clipboard into the message box with ⇧⌘V, never its images or attachments. The text replaces any selection and keeps its line breaks. If the clipboard holds no text, nothing is pasted and a notice says why. Works in the message box only, in bb Desktop on macOS. Requires bb 0.46+ and Plugin SDK 0.6.49+.

play-continue.description: Stop a run with a double Escape and pick up a stopped turn with one Play click. Two Escape presses within 400 ms press BB's own Stop button, and the Stop icon shows Esc after the first press. After a stopped, failed or restart-interrupted turn, Play replaces the disabled Send button and asks the agent to continue, checking state before repeating uncertain actions. No account, service or settings.

plugin-updates.description: Shows which installed plugins have updates and installs them for you, including newer releases outside a plugin's version range. A count on the nav icon and a one-time toast flag each new version. Compatible updates install in place, singly or all at once; out-of-range ones reinstall at the new release with settings restored and rollback on failure. Requires git and network access to each plugin's repository.

plugin-workshop.description: Turns a few sentences into an installed bb plugin, with one agent per stage from spec and mockup to code, review and rollout.

pokecut-theme.description: Turns bb into a soft dashboard: a gray shell, the thread as a raised panel, white cards and a pink-violet accent, light and dark. The composer gets even chips for project, machine and access, a gradient send button and a context line that fills as the window does. Expanded work groups read as one card with right-aligned durations and red error chips, and messages show their time on hover. A footer switch flips light, dark or system, and each chat feature can be turned off in English or Russian settings.

pokemon.description: Build your Pokémon collection as you finish work in BB. Archive a thread to catch one of 1,025 species, then track your progress and duplicate catches in the Pokédex. Explore each catch’s artwork, types, stats, abilities, and cry. Uses free PokeAPI data and GitHub-hosted media.

pokemon-catcher.description: Turn shipped engineering work into Pokémon catches, evolutions, and a collection that grows across BB threads. Earn rewards from local branches and worktrees, or selected GitHub repositories and Shortcut, Jira, or GitHub Issues. Choose any catch as an evolving companion, incubate Eggs through token usage, and filter the collection by type, rarity, generation, or shiny status. GitHub, Shortcut, and Jira connections require user-supplied credentials; the plugin also requests data, sprites, and cries from PokéAPI-hosted services. Requires BB 0.43+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.87+.

polza.description: Run bb threads on polza.ai models and pay in rubles from one Polza balance. Sign in with your Polza account; the plugin stores the issued key on the bb server. Choose which catalog models the picker offers, in your order, with prices and context size shown. The sidebar shows the available balance and the key's remaining spend limit, and each thread shows an estimated spend and cache hit rate above the composer. Polza also works as bb's AI service for thread titles and commit messages on a small model you choose. Threads run the Claude Code CLI against Polza, so Claude Code's tools, permission modes, plan mode and skills keep working; the plugin installs the CLI when it is missing. Needs a Polza account with balance.

pr-notes.description: Review pull requests, keep private notes, and chat with agents in BB. Find assigned PRs and review requests, inspect diffs and check results, and post comments or manage PRs using your GitHub access. PR details and saved notes become context in BB's native chat. Requires GitHub CLI signed in on the BB server; chat needs a configured agent provider and may incur its charges.

pr-xray.description: Understand a pull request before you judge it. PR X-ray groups the diff by concern and puts it in reading order, then explains it with a walkthrough, diagrams and the spots worth a closer look. Ask questions as you read, and comment or submit your review on GitHub without leaving bb.

preset-buttons.description: Starts a new thread on the harness you meant to use, not the one the last thread left behind. Four buttons in the New thread composer apply a saved provider, model, and reasoning level in one click. A settings editor builds the buttons from BB's live provider catalogue, so no JSON and no reload. The strip holds one row beside the project picker and never wraps.

preset-sync.description: Synchronizes portable BB plugins and settings across computers through a Git repository.

prime-agent-acp.description: Runs bb threads on Prime Agent (by Prime Intellect) through its native ACP protocol, with model discovery and reasoning level support. Installing the provider requires an explicit `bb prime-agent install` command that downloads and installs the official prime-agent binary from Prime Intellect; thread content is processed by Prime Intellect.

productive.description: Work a Productive.io board without leaving BB, and hand a ticket to an agent in one click. Kanban lanes group by workflow status or by task list, so the columns match the board you already use, and dragging a card writes the change back to Productive. Start a thread from any ticket, optionally in its own git worktree, with the ticket's fields as context. Agents reach the same board through a `bb productive` command. Needs a Productive.io account and an API token.

progressive-skill.description: Smart skill index compaction — usage-ranked, budget-capped skill lists so agents load the right skills.

project-explorer.description: Browse and edit the files behind a thread in the side panel, with git status colouring every name the way VS Code does. Modified files read amber, new files green, deleted red, and a collapsed folder inherits the colour of whatever changed inside it. Saving sends back the hash the file had when you opened it, so a change an agent made underneath you reports a conflict instead of being overwritten. Dotfiles such as .claude and .env appear, and directories load one level at a time, so a repository with node_modules opens as quickly as an empty one. Needs a thread whose environment has a workspace; git colours need that workspace to be a git repository.

project-folders.description: Organize BB chats into projects and nested sections that are real folders, so each chat starts in its own working directory. Each project and section can carry AGENTS.md rules from shared or own templates, plus custom rules for files or BB sessions and a startup instruction for new chats. Style the sidebar tree with 118 icons or any emoji, 12 colors, fills and four presets, per level, per project or per section. Archive finished sections with their files and chats and restore them later, keep working copies on several devices, and move projects or sections without breaking existing chats. Requires BB 0.43+ and macOS or Linux devices; the interface comes in 11 languages with English by default.

project-instructions.description: Gives each bb project its own standing instructions and adds them to the system prompt of every thread in that project, without writing anything into the repository.

project-page.description: Open a project's homepage from its name in BB's sidebar. The homepage renders the checkout's README, links to the configured repository, and starts a new thread in that project. Reads go through BB's project APIs and the project's enrolled host, so a remote browser client sees the same README as a local window. The sidebar chevron still expands and collapses threads, and disabling the plugin restores the original sidebar. Requires BB 0.43.1 or later with Plugin SDK 0.4.87 or later.

project-themes.description: Give every project its own color, so threads and workspaces are easier to recognize at a glance. Tint thread rows, browser tabs, and the workspace background independently. Choose from eight presets or a custom color; settings sync across bb windows. Requires bb 0.45 or later and no external service.

project-usage-sort.description: Puts the projects you work in most at the top of bb's project lists, re-ranked every hour from your own thread activity. Each thread counts toward its project, and its weight halves every 14 days, so this week's work outranks last quarter's. The order lands in bb's own project order, which the new-thread project picker uses, and in the built-in sidebar's project sections. Run bb project-usage-sort preview to see the ranking before anything moves; it runs on your bb server and calls no external service.

prompt-enhancer.description: Rewrites the composer draft into a clearer prompt through a hidden bb thread, keeping follow-ups short, preserving @mentions and file paths, and offering Undo.

prompts.description: Stashes prompts you write while an agent is busy and injects, schedules, or auto-sends them when it next goes idle, alongside a searchable snippet library with {{fill-in}} templates.

provider-brand-marks.description: Draws each provider logo in its own brand colour — Anthropic clay, OpenAI green, Pi steel blue, Hermes ultramarine — instead of the one monochrome mask they all share. Fits every colour to the palette you already use, in light and dark mode, without replacing your theme.

provider-muse.description: Adds Meta's Muse Code as a bb provider over its own session protocol: streamed timeline, approvals, subagents, model picker, health, and the plan's own 5-hour and weekly usage limits as Muse reports them.

provider-retry-advanced.description: Keeps BB's bundled overload and subscription-limit retries and resumes turns after lost connectivity. Optional, off by default: Claude Code UltraCode workflow recovery, a stalled-turn watchdog and continuation follow-ups. A fresh install observes until armed. Disable the bundled Provider retry before use.

provider-usage.description: Shows how much of each provider's plan is left — every rate-limit window, percent remaining, and when it resets, including Muse Code's 5-hour and weekly limits — plus a 7/30/90-day token chart covering every provider, from local transcripts and BB's own usage events.

pstack.description: Puts 47 pstack engineering skills in every bb thread, with one setup step to choose the models they delegate to. Run /setup-pstack once and it reads this host's model list, then asks which model each pstack role should use. After that, /poteto-mode loads one of 23 playbooks and runs the other skills its steps need: reviews that put a second model on the change, tests, blast-radius checks, and prose cleanup. Every skill has its own switch, and none reach the model prompt until you invoke them. Needs bb 0.43 or newer, the bb CLI for skills that fan out to workers, and MCP servers or a webhook endpoint for the few skills that ask for them.

pulse.description: See what needs you from Slack, Gmail and Calendar on one live board, kept current by scheduled agent runs. Hourly, Daily and Weekly runs write items sorted into Now, Next, Later and Nice to Know, and Done or Snooze sticks across runs. Each item can carry prepared replies that copy to your clipboard and open the source; nothing is sent for you. A robot button hands an item to an agent thread that drafts the work for your review. Your agents need their own Slack, Gmail and Calendar access (MCP servers, CLIs or plugins), and every run uses your model quota.

qlik-sense.description: Agents read Qlik Sense Enterprise sheets and charts with filters. Sign in once, tick the reports agents may use, and choose which models may see the data.

quick-chat.description: Ask a question in a floating chat window without adding a thread to your sidebar. Open it with Mod+Shift+K, the command palette, or the sidebar chat icon, and drag it to a convenient corner. Return to recent chats or choose Open as thread when a conversation becomes project work. Uses your configured BB agent provider and its account; provider usage charges or subscription limits still apply.

quick-compose.description: Start a thread from a floating composer without leaving the page you’re on. Open it with Mod+Shift+L, or hand off the current thread with Mod+Shift+H; both shortcuts can be rebound in Settings → Keyboard. Keep your draft and selections when you dismiss it, then start the thread in the background when you’re ready. Requires BB 0.42+ and uses your configured agent provider and account.

quick-reply.description: Give your agent quick feedback by clicking on which lines you agree and disagree with. Ask for more detail on any line, or add a comment when a click isn't enough.
quick-reply.licenseNote: в package.json указано "GPL-3.0-only", в репозитории GPL-3.0

quick-thread.description: Opens a floating new-thread composer from anywhere with Ctrl/Cmd+N, so you can start a thread without leaving the one you are on. Enter creates and opens it; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter creates it in the background and shows a toast with an Open action. A command-palette row covers keyboards where the OS reserves the shortcut.

qwen-cli.description: Code with your Qwen account inside BB. Choose CLI-discovered models, switch between Plan and Build, and review tool requests in your thread. Requires a separately installed Qwen Code CLI and an eligible account; service quota or charges apply.

rad-binder.description: Turn bb into an 80s/90s school-binder cover, with neon confetti, striped edges and chunky toy-commercial shadows. The sidebar becomes a deep-purple binder spine where the open thread is a hot-pink sticker. The composer, your messages and inline cards get thick outlines and hard offset shadows, and headings switch to bold italic capitals. Works in light and dark, makes no network requests, and uses Futura and Avenir Next from macOS, falling back to your system sans elsewhere.

radar.description: See every pull request and issue that needs you, live in the sidebar, on GitHub and Delta, plus optional read-only Gitstream history. Saved lanes are queried live through your gh and dt CLIs, and config and caches stay in bb on your machine. Describe a queue in plain words and bb's configured AI drafts the lane; Focus hides repos everywhere and single items can be hidden too. From any row, start a review or triage thread with Radar's skills attached or rebase your own PR. Optional Context from Slack summarises the public Slack threads that link an item.

radar-sidebar.description: See which threads need you without opening each conversation. Group threads by activity, project or section, fold nested families, and preview goals and context usage on hover. Filter or save views, use keyboard and bulk actions, and keep navigation aligned with BB's sidebar settings. Requires BB 0.44+ and uses exclusive experimental sidebar slots; no external service or account.

read-aloud.description: Listen to any assistant message while you keep working, with speech that starts playing before the whole message is synthesized. A speaker button on every message row starts playback, and the player adds pause, stop, ten-second skips in both directions, and speeds from 0.75x to 2x that persist between sessions. Playback stops on its own when you switch threads or send a new prompt, and stopping cancels the synthesis stream instead of leaving it to finish unheard. Code blocks, link targets, and bare URLs are flattened out of the text first, so a voice reads prose instead of syntax. Speech uses Microsoft Edge's public neural voices over the network, so it needs an internet connection, but no account, API key, or paid service.

realtime-gateway.description: Runs Voice Mode's realtime sessions through a Vercel AI Gateway key, so voice bills to one gateway account and the bb host never needs an OpenAI key. Voice Mode asks installed connection plugins for a session; this one mints a single-use client secret from the gateway and returns its realtime URL with the secret already attached to the WebSocket handshake. Pick the model (gpt-realtime-mini by default), set an optional team scope, and run bb realtime-gateway test to confirm the handshake before relying on it. Needs a Vercel AI Gateway key with usage billing; no OpenAI key on this host.

receipts.description: Compare coding-agent token usage and estimated API cost in one dashboard. Switch between 7, 30 and 90 days, with daily charts and breakdowns by model, project and day. Reads Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode and Pi usage from the bb server machine. Optional Cursor support requires a signed-in Cursor desktop app and its dashboard service; estimates are not subscription invoices.

reclaim.description: Find what filled your disk and get the space back, without guessing. Indexes the whole volume with no scan cap and counts hardlinks and APFS clones once, so shared copies do not inflate folder totals. Browse any folder by real subtree size, or work from a costed list of build output, idle dependencies, package caches, Xcode derived data and Docker layers, including compacting the Docker VM disk image that pruning alone never shrinks. Deletion is confined to roots you authorize, and a guard can clean up or hand the problem to an agent when space runs low. macOS and Linux, no account or external service.

rephrase.description: Adds a Re-phrase button to the prompt input that rewrites your draft with an agent and puts the result back in the composer.

responsibilities.description: Find failures, questions and unread results in BB. Filter threads, start child threads and optionally highlight managers.

retitle.description: Gives each thread a title that matches the conversation, not only its first message. After the first reply, a small model writes a new title: Haiku 4.5 on Claude Code, gpt-5.4-mini on Codex. Press ⌘⌥R, click the header button, or use the quick palette to rename any thread again, and turn on an emoji at the start of each title. Each rename runs one short session on the thread's own provider, so it needs no API key.

rewind.description: Undo an agent's file changes turn by turn, and let the conversation go back with them. Checkpoints the workspace before each message and after each turn, on every provider, with no setup. Preview a restore as a per-file diff before it runs, and undo it afterwards. Restore the files and edit your message in one step, or fork from any message into a worktree whose files are as they were then. Flags turns that ran git push, a deploy, or other effects a restore cannot undo. Needs git on the thread's machine; the workspace itself does not have to be a git repository.

role-picker.description: Choose a specialist in the composer without leaving the conversation. Includes six built-in roles and optionally connects to Agent Roles for custom profiles. Agent work uses your configured provider account and quota.

route.description: Hand mechanical edits to a cheaper agent, ask another model, or get a ranked decision without leaving the turn. route_worker runs a task on any BB harness and model you list, in the same environment, and returns its final message. route_ask sends one prompt to any OpenAI-compatible API, and route_decide asks a System One decision model such as TypeSafe Jev for a pick with probabilities. Each tool needs its own provider or endpoint and key, billed by that service.

save-my-model.description: Give every BB machine its own provider, model, and reasoning preference. Configure each machine through BB's native picker and review or clear browser-local records without changing the built-in New Thread defaults.

scoped-skills.description: Give each skill only to the agents, models and projects that should have it, so image skills reach Codex and stay out of Claude Code. Each skill carries a list of agents plus optional model and project globs such as gpt-5* or *my-org/*, and a thread receives only the skills that match its agent, model and project. A preview shows what a thread on any agent, model and project would get. Import skill folders from the BB machine, or ask a thread to list or change a scope; a bb scoped-skills CLI does the same. Needs no account, API key or network access.

screen-sharing.description: See and control the screens of your Macs from inside bb, at your desk or from anywhere through your getbb.app address. A sidebar page shows each Mac connected to your bb with whether its Screen Sharing is on, and opens its screen in the page for your keyboard and mouse. Sessions to several Macs can be open at once, with View only, Send keys for shortcuts such as Command-Tab, Full screen, and a Clipboard menu that sends text either way or keeps both clipboards in sync, for the macOS account bb runs as on that Mac. Every new session asks for that Mac's own macOS user name and password, which bb never keeps, and a Close all pill ends every session at once. Requires bb 0.47 or later and macOS, with Screen Sharing turned on by you in System Settings on each Mac; it relies on experimental bb plugin APIs that may change between bb releases.

section-load-more.description: Keep long sidebar sections short, so opening one never pushes the others out of view. Each custom section and the Threads group shows its first 10 threads, with Load more and Show less at the end of the same section. Nothing is archived or moved, and the thread you have open always stays visible. Set the starting count and the batch size in the plugin settings.

security-guidance.description: Pattern-matched security warnings for code the agent writes — 25 rules covering unsafe deserialization, injection, XSS, and crypto footguns.

sentry-issues.description: Browses bounded, read-only Sentry issue snapshots across configured projects and opens searchable issue detail with optional local BB triage links.

server-status.description: Tracks host RAM usage as a ring around a sidebar footer button — amber from 80%, red above 90% — and opens a panel with CPU, memory, swap, disk, load average, uptime, and OS and kernel version.

session-history.description: See every Claude Code, Codex and Qwen Code session you ran outside BB, under the titles the agents gave them. The new-thread screen lists the sessions from the selected project's folders, and a Sessions page lists all of them with agent filters and search. Open any session to read its transcript, show its tool calls, or copy the command that resumes it in a terminal. Session files are read on the machine that runs BB and are never uploaded or changed.

session-log.description: Check what an agent actually ran, changed and decided, in one live log beside the chat. Messages, thinking, commands with their output and exit codes, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps appear in timeline order, with a timestamp on every row and a duration on every command. The log follows new output as it arrives, opens failed commands by default, and filters to messages, thinking, tools or errors. Search covers the whole session, and single keys jump between rows, replies and errors. Open it with Mod+Shift+L or from the thread header; it reads bb's timeline and keeps no copy of the thread.

session-notes.description: Attaches private, thread-scoped notes to individual bb timeline messages, and never sends them to the agent's context.

sessions-switcher.description: Switch between seven recent sessions with Alt+Tab-style controls. Hold the shortcut modifier, select with the keyboard or pointer, then release to open. Choose horizontal cards or a vertical list, with provider icons and live running and unread indicators. No extra account or service is required.

shell-tasks.description: Keep agents moving while tests, builds, servers and watchers run in the background. Track each command in its thread, read live output, stop its process group and clear it when finished. Tasks survive plugin reloads, and successful or failed jobs can wake the agent with one batched completion message. Requires BB 0.43+, Plugin SDK 0.5.9+ and a Unix execution machine; commands run through `/bin/sh` with no external account.

shop-kanban.description: Shows your bb threads as cards placed by live state, so you see at a glance which ones need you. Cards move on their own: a pending question or a failed run turns red at the top of Working, a reply that reports completion lands in Done, and threads you set aside wait in Parked. A working limit caps how many threads run at once: past it, a new thread waits in Queue and starts when a working one finishes, to pace spend. Each card carries a model-written title and summary, context-window fill, the harness icon, and the cost of the thread together with every child thread and subagent it started. Queue's In tab lists the Delta and GitHub pull requests waiting on you or your teams, each with a risk chip, approve and request-changes buttons, and a drafted thread that explains the change, and the Out tab tracks your own open and merged pull requests. The title bar searches every thread by what was said in it, archived ones included, and shows CPU, memory, disk and battery with the heaviest apps; on a Shopify account it also shows today's Shopify AI proxy spend. Titles, summaries and risk chips come from a pi-compatible CLI on the thread's host (default Claude Haiku 4.5), billed to that CLI's account; search needs qmd and the pull request lists need the dt or gh CLI, signed in, on a persistent host. Each is optional.

shortcut.description: Turn your assigned Shortcut stories into agent work in bb. Browse and reorder stories on a Kanban board, filter by workflow, and read story details. Start work from a story to move it to In Development and open an agent thread. Requires a Shortcut account and API token.

show-latest-threads.description: Shows only the threads you touched in the last 24, 48 or 72 hours, so the sidebar holds today's work. A switch and a 24h / 48h / 72h picker sit at the top of the list; turn the switch off to see every project. Pinned threads, sections and child threads keep their places, and a thread that is open, running or waiting for your answer stays visible whatever its age. Each row shows its status on the right as BB's own list does: a dot for unread, a spinner while the agent works, a question mark when it waits for you. English or Russian.

shuttle.description: Puts every pull request that needs you, from any server, in one Inbox grouped by what to do next. Each of your PRs keeps an agent thread that gets its new reviews, comments and failed checks, and fixes them or just passes them on. AI reviews come back as drafts you edit and post as yourself, and auto post, in shadow mode for the repositories you pick, records which findings it would have posted. Saved boards keep the PRs of a release or a handoff together with live status, across repositories and servers. Merge, comment, reply and resolve from Shuttle, with merges and reviews queued in the background on each server. GitHub works through your signed-in gh CLI; GitLab and other servers need a command adapter, a few shell commands you write that print JSON.

side-board.description: See every question, bug and todo your agent raises in one panel beside the thread, so nothing gets lost in the scroll. Items are numbered Q1, B1, T1: answer in chat with "Q3 clerk", or "go" to accept every recommendation. Agents add and close items themselves through the board_add and board_close tools, in every thread and with every provider. If a reply asks a question or finishes work without updating the board, the agent gets one reminder; you can turn this off in settings.

side-chat-links.description: Reopen a side chat from the message you started it on, instead of hunting for it. A thread icon appears under every message that has side chats, with a count when there are several. Click it to open a panel tab for that message, with one inner tab for each of its side chats. Rename a side chat by double-clicking its tab. Works with bb's bundled Side chat plugin, including side chats made before you install it, and needs bb 0.49 or later.

sidebar-plus.description: Keep active projects within reach and check thread status without leaving the sidebar. Pin, hide, reorder, and search projects in collapsible sections. Inspect branch and pull request details from thread menus, where you can also open a split, mark threads read or unread, pin, rename, archive, or delete them. Preferences stay in sync across BB windows.

sidebar-subtitles.description: Group sidebar destinations under your own headings. Drag sections or move them with arrow controls, hide sections and restore them from More. Edit headings with explicit Save, Cancel and Delete controls; your BB navigation order and visibility are preserved.

simple-sidebar-folders.description: Fold whole groups of sidebar projects, so work projects stay out of sight at home and personal ones stay out of sight at work. Drag a project by its name onto a folder to file it; BB's own project and thread rows stay as they are. A folded folder shows how many projects it holds, and a dot when a thread in it needs you. Folders are shared across your BB clients, and each client remembers which ones it keeps folded.

simple-summaries.description: Keep the latest thread summary in view as small italic text above the composer. Read the full summary with natural wrapping and no widget controls or badges. Generate summaries on demand or automatically after a thread becomes idle. Requires a configured BB provider and model; generation uses its normal subscription allowance or API billing.

skill-manager.description: Keep agent skills in sync from one hub. Find skills on skills.sh, install into selected agents, compare local copies, and check for updates. Requires Git and internet access for downloads and update checks.

skills.description: See every skill a thread's agent can use, where each one comes from and what it says, and add one to the chat from the panel or composer. A Skills tab in the thread's side panel groups them by origin — the project, the repository, your personal folder, an admin folder, a Claude Code or Codex plugin, or bb itself — and shows each one's SKILL.md, rendered, with its path on disk. Claude Code, Codex and Hermes threads have their skill folders read the way that agent reads them, in worktrees and on other enrolled machines too, so a name defined twice is listed once, under the copy the agent uses. Add to chat puts the skill in the message box as the same pill bb's / menu inserts and sends nothing, and a Skills button with a live count, or a keyboard command, opens the same list in bb's pop-up above the message box. Threads on other providers list bb's own skills and what bb's / menu offers. Needs bb 0.45 or later, and no account, key or network access.

slopcop.description: Automated PR review rules that dispatch BB agents.

sops.description: A SOPS editor for BB: see a repo's encrypted files, edit them in a table or as text, and save them encrypted again. Needs sops installed.
sops.licenseNote: в package.json указано "GPL-3.0-only", в репозитории GPL-3.0

souls.description: Give any thread a persona you define once: its job, voice, expertise and hard limits, the same in every thread that runs it. An agent interviews you in four to seven questions and puts the draft on a review card, and nothing is saved, edited or deleted until you approve. Pick a soul from the composer's + menu for an open thread or the next one, and a banner shows it with a pixel-art portrait that animates with what the agent is doing. After a context compaction the persona goes back in, and a parent thread can start a child already in character. Compare a soul with no soul on the same prompt before you rely on it. Souls stay in the plugin's own SQLite store with no account or external service, and a comparison spends model runs only when you start it.

spaces.description: Show only the projects you are working on by switching the sidebar between spaces such as Work and Personal. Each space has a name, an icon, its own projects and an optional sidebar tint; pick one from the menu in the sidebar header or press Ctrl+Alt+1 to 9 (⌃⌥ on macOS), and it reopens the thread you last had open there. All projects shows everything again. Edit Spaces sets each space's projects, icon, tint and order, turns folders dragged in from Explorer or Finder into projects, and keeps a project in no space visible in every space. `bb space` switches from a terminal or an agent. Needs bb 0.49 or later with the bundled Thread list plugin, and an active space groups the thread list by project.

specs.description: Give every project one shared set of spec documents that agents read before they change code. Specs link to any number of projects and live in one store, so they survive branches, worktrees, and new checkouts. Each project thread receives a compact index of its specs — pinned documents always, changed documents when they changed — and pulls full text only when an agent asks. Select a quote to leave a comment; open comments come back from the read tool as review feedback instead of silent edits. Every spec gets its own chat thread where the agent reads before answering and applies agreed changes with a revision check. Agents also get the bb specs command line and tools for search, annotate, attach, detach, and delete. Runs entirely inside BB: no account and no external service.

sql.description: Browse every Postgres database, complete SQL with schema awareness, and run queries from a panel or agent tools. New connections default to Agent write and Allow DDL on; duplicate connections from the menu.

steel-browser.description: Operate self-hosted Steel browser sessions from BB with project-scoped sessions, selectable Playwright or Jev execution, and inline viewing.

sticky-prompt.description: Keeps your message pinned at the top of the chat, so you always know which question a long reply answers. As soon as your message scrolls up, a two-line copy stays above the reply, drawn with BB's own Markdown, and your next message pushes it away. Click it to jump back to the full message, even in a long thread where BB has unloaded it. Images show as thumbnails, short turns are left alone, and messages from agents and BB notices are skipped unless you turn them on. Runs in the BB app with your own session and needs no account or external service.

stl-preview.description: Inspect STL models beside your BB conversation. Orbit, pan and zoom, switch to wireframe, and read dimensions and triangle counts. Open workspace, host and thread-storage files through BB, including selected remote hosts. Requires WebGL2; supports binary and ASCII STL up to 64 MiB and one million triangles, with no separate viewer or external service.

subscription-pace.description: See whether every AI subscription you pay for will last until it renews. Tracks Vercel Token Pass and OpenCode Go live, and takes any other plan in the three free slots, then draws them all on one percent-of-allowance chart with a forecast to each renewal. There is no combined percentage: a headline that averages plans needs a weight for each, and OpenCode's limit is a per-model figure the endpoint does not name, so any weight would be a guess. Instead the panel counts the subscriptions in trouble — over the limit, or on pace to be before they reset. A provider that cannot be read shows as unreadable rather than as zero, and nothing is guessed: allowances start from a suggestion you confirm.

subthread-columns.description: Answer waiting subthreads and inspect failures beside their parent. Optional Responsibilities adds unread-result columns.

switchboard.description: See which agent threads failed, need you or are still running, grouped under your bb sections. Child threads nest under their parent across projects, and a collapsed parent still shows its most urgent child. A status-lanes view lists every awake thread under Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle. Drag threads to reorder, nest or move them between sections, and snooze a quiet family until tomorrow morning. Hover a row for the thread's model, context use, branch, uncommitted changes and pull request. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each bb client.

syns.description: Lets the pages your agents write read and save your Syns files, so a task board or wiki on a page is the repository itself, not a copy. A page sees only the repository, or the placed folder, its session works in, with the access of the Syns account signed in on that machine. Every edit carries the version the page last read: if the files moved since, the edit is refused and the page re-reads, so an edit never overwrites changes it hasn't seen. From a control you press, a page can also share a folder, set its visibility and manage who has access. Needs Thread Pages 1.10.0 or later, and the Syns CLI installed and signed in to a Syns account on each machine whose sessions use it.

system-messages-tab.description: Keeps "Your messages" in the thread outline to what you typed, moving BB notices and messages from other threads into their own tab. In an orchestrator thread with child agents, that took one outline from 1,045 entries to the 78 the user wrote. Every tab lists the newest message first, every outline entry gets a date and time, and senders the outline would label "Agent" show their thread title. A BB update can hide these changes until the plugin catches up; the outline keeps working.

t3-import.description: Bring your T3 Code threads into bb and pick up each conversation where you left off. Each thread lands in the bb project for its folder with its messages, reasoning, tool calls, plans, and dates, and the next message continues with the agent's full context. A preview lists every thread and project before anything changes, settled threads can come over archived, and each import backs up the bb database first. Requires bb 0.45, with T3 Code and Claude Code or Codex on the same computer; the plugin writes threads directly to the bb database.

t3sidebar.description: Replaces the BB thread list with a stable inbox, snooze controls, and child thread links.

tab-close-right.description: Keep tab icons visible and close tabs from the right. Active tabs always show their close button; other tabs reveal it on hover or keyboard focus without shifting the title. Touch screens show the button without hover. Requires BB 0.46.1+; future BB layout changes may require an update.

table-expand.description: Opens any markdown table in a thread full width, the way bb already expands images and Mermaid diagrams. Click the table or its corner expand button to see it in a dialog at the window width, with cells wrapping and both axes scrolling when it is still too big. Links, buttons and text selections inside the table keep working; Esc, the close button or the backdrop closes it. Relies on bb's table markup, so a bb update can break it until the plugin catches up.

tabs.description: Keep work and home conversations separate and return to the chats you need. Switch workspaces with independent pins and favorites, and restore your last local choice when reopening BB. Search chats and projects, explore nested chats in side menus, and customize project aliases and tab colors. Supports 15 interface languages; requires BB 0.43+ with no external service or account.

taskboard.description: Browses and creates project-scoped GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Linear, or Jira issues in one focused List or Kanban board, with explicit review before creation and an optional autonomous task factory.

tasks-kanban.description: Turn BB's built-in Tasks into a live Kanban board: drag cards across all six statuses, create, edit, comment, and label tasks. Every change goes straight into the Tasks tracker that bb tasks and agents use, so the board never drifts from the data. Works with any tracker project; Russian and English UI.

team.description: Agent teams with a shared Beads or built-in task tracker, reusable roles, safe session handoffs, review gates and finite execution budgets. Edit team templates, select approved models and follow task ownership and session status in one panel. Requires BB 0.49 or newer; Beads mode additionally requires bd 1.3.1.

telegram-projects.description: Get BB agent reports in Telegram and answer any thread from your phone, one topic per project. When an agent finishes, waits for you or stops, its project topic gets a card with the section, thread and agent, and the reply collapsed or summarized by a BB model you choose. Connect the reported thread with one tap and keep working with that agent by text or voice. Pick which agent and Tasks events arrive, with or without sound, and use the bot in Russian or English. Requires your own Telegram bot; messages of connected chats and reports are sent to Telegram.

terminal-jobs.description: Runs terminal commands that outlive agent turns, keeps job records and output logs, and sends completion notices to the owning BB thread.

terminal-toggle.description: Toggle the last focused native terminal with Ctrl+backtick. Press again to hide the panel and return to the composer.

terminals.description: Open shells on any machine connected to bb from one sidebar page, and find them still running when you come back. Each tab is a terminal in that machine's home folder, with no project, thread or checkout needed; with several machines connected, the + button lists them so you pick one. Tabs reattach to their shells after a reload, the desktop app and bb in a browser show and type into the same shells, and a machine that goes offline picks up where it was when it reconnects. Select text in a terminal to put it in an open or new thread's message box as terminal output, for you to send yourself. Requires bb 0.48 or later and at least one machine connected to bb; a terminal runs that machine's own shell as the user bb runs as there.

theme-toggle.description: Flips bb between light and dark from a sidebar footer button: a click switches the appearance, while hovering, holding, or right-clicking opens a menu with light, dark, or system appearance and every palette installed on the host, including ones other plugins provide. The icon is a square split by a diagonal — day above, night below — and the half that is on is filled.

thread-images.description: Shows every image an agent opens right in the thread. Click one to see it full size. An Images gallery in the thread context card keeps every image from the thread, newest first. Works the same in Claude Code, Codex, ACP and Pi threads.

thread-namer.description: Names threads with an agent when their first turn ends, so the sidebar reads as what you were doing, and re-generates a name on demand from the thread header or the CLI.

thread-names.description: Names each thread "category: name" in lowercase, like "fix: login redirect loop", so a long sidebar reads at a glance. Eight categories for coding work come built in, and the settings page takes up to 16 of your own plus sample names in the style you want. Once you pick it as the thread-title service in bb settings, a thread whose title is not yet in that form gets a new one after a finished turn, at most twice. A thread you rename by hand after it got such a name keeps your title. Titles come from bb cloud, so the plugin needs a signed-in bb account with bb cloud on, and each title uses its daily AI budget; it needs no API key.

thread-pages.description: Gives every agent session a web page it writes for its task, and lets you answer from that page instead of chat. Each page is built for the task at hand: a diagram you click, a decision sheet, a report that shows what failed. Your choices and notes on the page arrive as the agent's next message, from bb or from your phone. A built-in home lists your sessions by what needs you and by project. Pages run sandboxed with no bb credentials, and anything that touches another session asks you first.

thread-reference.description: Bring a BB thread's current context into another conversation without copying its transcript. Drop a sidebar thread directly into the composer, or choose one from the Threads mention provider. References stay clickable in sent messages so you can return to the source thread. The plugin reads source threads without modifying them.
